# [80/159] Theses/AIXA - Aixtron.md
**thesis · ticker: AIXA · status: active · conviction: medium · sector: Semiconductor Capital Equipment · date: 2026-04-29 · metrics as of: 2026-08-16 · tags: thesis, semiconductors, AIXA, MOCVD, photonics · source: https://www.aixtron.com/en/investors**

## Summary

Aixtron is being repriced from a cyclical SiC/GaN power-equipment supplier into the dominant MOCVD toolmaker for the InP photonics buildout, but the market has not yet underwritten how complete the application mix has flipped: optoelectronics moved from 12% of equipment revenue in 2024 to 23% in 2025, and Q1 2026 order intake hit 65% optoelectronics, a structural transition compressed into four quarters. The thesis is that AIXA captures a near-monopolistic share of a multi-year InP capacity wave (Lumentum Greensboro, Coherent, Nokia G10-AsP, SMART Photonics, plus three undisclosed leading laser makers) at the same time GaN-on-Si data-center power demand layers on as an independent second leg via NVIDIA's 800V transition expected in 2027. Despite a +138% YTD rally to €41 (~€4.7B) and Q1 2026's -38% EBIT operating deleverage (revenue €59.4M), NTM P/E is ~55x on trough FY2026E €0.74 EPS: the mix-shift is in the NTM multiple. On FY2027E €1.34 consensus the stock is still ~31x, inside the SiC-equipment 30-40x band, vs LITE/COHR at 48-60x: the gap is now a 2027-earnings claim, not an NTM one. The market still prices AIXA as a SiC equipment cycle name with a photonics call option rather than a photonics enabler with a SiC tail. Initial conviction medium pending Apr 30 Q1 2026 results validating mix-shift durability, FY guide reaffirmation, and free cash flow trajectory.

## Key Non-consensus Insights

**The mix shift is the thesis, and it is already happening, not a 2027+ option**: Sell-side consensus models AIXA as a cyclical SiC/GaN power-equipment supplier with a photonics adjacency. The 2024→2025 application-split data ruptures that framing: power equipment fell from 55% to 50% of mix while optoelectronics doubled from 12% to 23%, and Q1 2026 prelim orders printed 65% optoelectronics share. The market is treating the FY2026 €560M ±€30M guide (raised Apr 14 from €520M; optically flat vs FY2025 €557M) as power-cycle softness, but the flat headline masks the compositional shift: management guided optoelectronics to more than double year-over-year into 2026, with declining SiC/LED offsetting it, so the revenue mix is inflecting even as the top line is not. The implication is that 2026 numbers will look like a typical "second leg of a SiC recovery" while the underlying revenue composition will be ~45-55% optoelectronics by year-end, and 2027 will land entirely under a different economic narrative the sell-side is not modeling. This is a business-mix transition pricing event, not a cycle-timing call.

**G10-AsP is the ASML of InP for the 6-inch wafer transition**: The InP industry is migrating from 3-inch and 4-inch wafers to 6-inch ([[Theses/LITE - Lumentum]] Greensboro fab is the canonical reference deployment), and 6-inch InP/AsP epitaxy requires reactor architectures the legacy 3/4-inch installed base cannot retrofit. Aixtron's G10-AsP platform is the only commercially shipping 6-inch InP MOCVD reactor at scale: Nokia's confirmed G10-AsP order, SMART Photonics' fab buildout, and three additional "leading laser maker" wins disclosed in the FY2025 results call effectively give Aixtron sole-source position for the 6-inch transition window. Veeco's Compound Semiconductor exposure (9% of 2025 revenue, guided to 12% in 2026E) is concentrated in mature LED and laser MOCVD on smaller wafer sizes; Veeco does not have a comparable 6-inch InP product on the market today. This is a 2-3 year window of vendor monoculture in the equipment that gates an entire industry transition, economically equivalent to ASML's EUV monopoly during the 7nm-to-5nm transition, scaled to a fraction of the absolute dollar TAM but with similar share dynamics.

**Headline MOCVD market share (VECO 28%, AIXA 24%) understates AIXA's dominance in the InP-specific segment by ~3x**: Public market-share data aggregates all MOCVD applications (LED, laser, power, photonics) into a single "MOCVD equipment" denominator, in which Veeco's mature LED-MOCVD installed base inflates its top-line share. Within InP/photonics-specific MOCVD, customer disclosures and equipment supplier audits put Aixtron at >70% share, and within the 6-inch InP subset specifically (G10-AsP class) the share is approximately 90%+. Kerrisdale Capital's published long thesis triangulates this from the customer side (Lumentum, Coherent, Nokia, SMART Photonics public capacity guidance + IQE epi-foundry buildout). The investor-bias error is that a sell-side analyst pulling "MOCVD market share" from Yole or Mordor Intelligence will see a balanced 24/28/48 (Aixtron / Veeco / others) split and conclude AIXA has commoditized competition risk, when the actual exposed segment AIXA is winning has near-monopoly economics. This understates both pricing power on incoming orders and gross margin defensibility through the cycle.

**AIXA is implicitly long LITE/COHR/NVDA at semis-cycle equipment multiples**: Aixtron sells the picks-and-shovels into the InP capacity wave that Lumentum, Coherent, IQE, and II-VI epi customers are building to feed NVIDIA's CPO transition and the broader 1.6T/3.2T optical transceiver upgrade. [[Theses/LITE - Lumentum]] currently trades at ~50x forward earnings on the high-conviction CPO/EML thesis; [[Theses/NVDA - Nvidia]] silicon photonics roadmap is priced at premium multiples. Aixtron, as the equipment supplier capturing first-dollar capacity capex (typically 18-24 months ahead of customer revenue ramp), trades at ~31x FY2027E consensus EPS (~55x NTM on trough FY2026E €0.74), still the SiC/GaN equipment-cycle band on 2027 earnings, not the NTM print. The 2027E valuation gap implies the market is pricing AIXA's photonics exposure at ~0% probability of materializing into the equipment book at scale, when the application-mix data already shows it has materialized. Re-rating to a photonics-equipment multiple (40-55x) on consensus 2027 EPS would imply 30-60% upside before any fundamental beat. The argument is direct multiple arbitrage between a customer that pays AIXA's invoices and AIXA itself, not a derivative valuation.

**800V data center power is a second independent demand leg, not photonics 2.0**: NVIDIA's 800V architecture transition (publicly targeted for 2027 GPU racks) requires GaN-on-Si and SiC power conversion stages with ~3x the device count of current 48V/54V systems, and current 200mm/300mm GaN-on-Si epi capacity is sized for consumer/auto applications rather than the AI data-center vertical at scale. AIXA's G10-SiC and AIX G5+C platforms are the dominant tools for the GaN-on-Si epi capacity that this requires. The non-consensus point is timing: photonics MOCVD orders are landing in 2026-2027 (capacity for 2028-2029 transceiver shipments), and 800V power MOCVD orders land later than first modeled: management (Feb 2026 FY25 call) said the 800V GaN ramp is "not there yet… still some time out into the future," framing it as a '27–'29 cycle rather than the late-2026/1H-2027 landing originally assumed. These are uncorrelated demand cycles drawing on the same equipment base, meaning AIXA's revenue growth path through 2027-2028 has two independent S-curves stacking rather than the single SiC-recovery curve sell-side currently models. The bear case requires both cycles to disappoint simultaneously, which has historically been rare.

## Outstanding Questions

**Will H2 2026 convert the €456.9M equipment backlog into the €386M of revenue the €560M guide still needs, or does the Q1 recognition gap return**: Q1 printed €59.4M revenue / -38% EBIT (not the €100-110M earlier drafts carried). Q2 did not repeat that print (€115.1M revenue, 13% EBIT), but H1 is still €174.5M / -4% EBIT against a ~€135M annual fixed-cost base that needs ~€135-140M/quarter to break even. Hitting €560M now requires ~€193M/quarter in H2 vs Q2's €115M; H1 orders €386M (+54% YoY) and FCF €162M say demand and cash are not the constraint. The bearish reading is that H2 recognition still slips and the guide is masking push-outs. Resolution: Q3 revenue vs the ~€193M run-rate.

**Is the FY2026 order book skewed toward 6-inch InP G10-AsP (high gross margin, low competitive risk) or toward power tools (commodity-like competition with VECO/CCS)**: Aixtron's FY2025 results presentation gave application split for revenue (50% power / 22% LED / 23% opto) but did not disclose the equivalent application split for the entering FY2026 order book. The Q1 2026 prelim 65% optoelectronics order share is encouraging but a single quarter, and InP-specific share within the optoelectronics bucket is not separately disclosed. The thesis economics depend heavily on this composition: an order book that is 50% G10-AsP InP photonics has structurally different gross margins (high 40s+) than one that is 50% G5/G6 SiC power (mid-30s, with VECO/CCS pricing competition). Resolution: management commentary at the Apr 30 call, May Investor Day if scheduled, or backed-out from segment gross margin trajectory through H1.

**How concentrated is the InP customer base, and what happens if Lumentum or Coherent push out 6-inch capacity decisions by 12-18 months**: Public customer disclosures suggest the Aixtron InP order book leans on Nokia G10-AsP, SMART Photonics, three undisclosed "leading laser makers" (likely some combination of Lumentum, Coherent, II-VI/Coherent, Marvell-via-IQE, Marvell direct), plus IQE as an epi-foundry layer. If two of the top five customers push out (e.g., LITE Greensboro phase-2 or COHR's Sherman buildout), 30-40% of the FY2027 order book could be at risk. The dependency risk is meaningful enough that customer concentration disclosure should drive sizing. Resolution: pull customer concentration disclosure from FY2025 20-F equivalent (German prospectus), cross-check against [[Theses/LITE - Lumentum]] capex guidance for 2027.

**Does AIXA have a credible defensive moat against an Asian (Tokuyama, Aixtron-China) or US (Veeco G10-equivalent) entrant in 6-inch InP MOCVD by 2028, or is the monopoly window 2-3 years before competition arrives**: ASML's EUV monopoly persisted because the underlying physics required components (collector mirrors, source plasma) that took competitors a decade to attempt, and they still failed. Aixtron's G10-AsP advantage on 6-inch InP MOCVD is process know-how (precursor chemistry control, multi-wafer reactor uniformity at 6-inch) plus customer integration cycles (3-6 months per fab qualification), which is real but order-of-magnitude shorter than ASML's moat. Veeco has signaled R&D priority on Compound Semiconductor and could ship a competitive 6-inch InP product in 18-24 months if the demand wave materializes at scale. The thesis time horizon for monopoly economics is therefore 2-3 years (2026-2028), with shared-vendor competitive economics post-2028 as the base case. This shapes terminal-value sizing significantly. Resolution: track Veeco's compound semiconductor R&D capex disclosure, conference talk titles, and customer dual-source qualifications announced in 2026-2027.

**What is the realistic NVIDIA 800V GaN-on-Si epi capacity adder to AIXA's order book in 2027, and is the 2027 timing dependent on NVIDIA Rubin/Rubin-Ultra ramping smoothly or could it slip to 2028**: NVIDIA's 800V transition timing has been publicly indicated as 2027 but is functionally tied to the Rubin and Rubin-Ultra GPU launch cadence, which has slipped before in NVIDIA's roadmap. If 800V slips to 2028, the GaN-on-Si capacity orders that AIXA models for 2H 2026 - 1H 2027 push out 4-6 quarters, materially impacting the second-leg revenue ramp. The InP photonics demand is more durable (driven by 1.6T optical, multiple silicon photonics roadmaps including [[Theses/AVGO - Broadcom]]'s, multiple end-customers) but the 800V leg is single-customer-driven. Resolution: track NVIDIA Rubin schedule commentary at GTC 2026 (June), Computex 2026, and any data-center power supplier disclosure (Vicor, Delta Electronics, Eaton).

**Is the Kerrisdale Capital long thesis (€1.4B 2029 revenue, €2 EPS 2028, 270% upside) a shared-information catalyst or has it already been priced into the +138% YTD rally**: Kerrisdale published the long thesis with detailed numerical targets in early 2026 and the stock has rallied +138% YTD, suggesting significant positioning has already moved. The risk is buying a thesis where the asymmetric upside has already been collected by early movers, leaving downside skew to disappointment scenarios. Counter-argument: if the operating mix-shift continues to print as observed in Q1 2026, the consensus EPS revisions ahead are still meaningfully ahead of current Bloomberg consensus, leaving 30-50% multiple-driven upside on top of any Kerrisdale-style numbers. Resolution: compare Aixtron 2027/2028 sell-side consensus EPS pre-Kerrisdale vs current vs Kerrisdale targets; gap closure rate over Q2-Q3 2026 is the read on whether the thesis is consensus or still emerging.

## Business Model & Product Description

Aixtron designs, manufactures, and supports MOCVD (Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition) systems, the deposition equipment used to grow compound semiconductor epitaxial layers (InP, GaAs, GaN, SiC, AlN) on wafer substrates. The business is structurally analogous to [[Sectors/Semiconductor Capital Equipment]] within compound semiconductors: Aixtron sells one-time capital equipment ($3-15M per tool) plus recurring revenue from spare parts, consumables, software upgrades, and service contracts that compound across the installed base. The SaaS analog is closer than typical equipment makers because each MOCVD tool ties the customer into Aixtron's recipe library, precursor qualification, and proprietary process recipes; switching cost is high enough that customer churn at the equipment level is rare even when competitor tools are nominally cheaper.

Three product platforms drive ~85% of revenue:

**G10-AsP (InP/GaAs/AsP photonics, 6-inch)**: The flagship 6-inch InP MOCVD reactor, the only commercially shipping platform at scale for the InP/AsP photonics 6-inch transition. Each tool is approximately €4-7M ASP, qualified for laser diodes (EML, DFB), photodetectors, semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOAs), and integrated photonic ICs. Customers include Nokia (announced), SMART Photonics (announced), three undisclosed leading laser/photonics customers (likely subset of Lumentum, Coherent, II-VI/Coherent, Marvell, IQE foundry layer). This platform is the InP/photonics revenue driver and the highest-margin product in the portfolio (estimated 45-55% gross margin).

**G10-SiC (Silicon Carbide power, 200mm)**: The 200mm SiC MOCVD platform serving EV power module manufacturers (BorgWarner, ON Semi, Wolfspeed, ROHM, Infineon partial). Each tool ~$3-5M ASP. This is the cyclical leg: strong 2022-2024 with the EV inflection, then normalized in 2025 with EV demand softness in China and Europe; recovery driven by Wolfspeed restructuring + ROHM India expansion + ON Semi Czech buildout in 2026-2027. SiC is more competitive than InP (Veeco Propel 200mm is direct competitor, plus Chinese entrants 3SBio, Naura at smaller scale). Estimated 30-40% gross margin.

**AIX G5+C and G4+C (GaN-on-Si and GaN-on-Sapphire, 200mm)**: Multi-wafer GaN platforms targeted at GaN-on-Si power electronics (data-center 800V, EV onboard chargers, fast-charging AC adapters) and the legacy GaN-on-Sapphire LED business. The data-center 800V demand layer is the new optionality: historically these tools served LED and consumer fast-charging; the 800V transition reframes them into AI infrastructure equipment. Each tool ~$2-4M ASP. Estimated 35-45% gross margin.

Revenue segmentation (FY2025 actuals):
- **Equipment**: ~€430M (~77% of total): new tool sales to compound semi fab customers.
- **Aftermarket/Service**: ~€127M (~23% of total): spare parts, service contracts, recipe library upgrades. Recurring, ~50% gross margin, growing in lockstep with installed base.

Application split of equipment revenue (FY2025): 50% Power (SiC/GaN-on-Si combined), 22% LED, 23% Optoelectronics (InP photonics + lasers), 5% Other. The Q1 2026 65% optoelectronics order intake share is the leading indicator that revenue mix flips materially in 2026-2027.

Geographic revenue mix (FY2025): ~45% Asia (Korea, China, Japan, Taiwan), ~30% Europe (Nokia, SMART Photonics, II-VI/Coherent Saxony fab), ~25% Americas (Lumentum Greensboro, Coherent Sherman, Wolfspeed). Asia weighting reflects China LED legacy + Korea/Taiwan compound semi foundry buildout.

Operating model: ~€135M annual fixed cost (R&D + SG&A + manufacturing overhead), capex €60-80M/year (R&D-intensive, including next-generation reactor platforms), free cash flow margin 12-18% in steady state, swinging materially negative in low-revenue quarters due to the high fixed-cost base. Cash+STI H1 2026 €816M against the inaugural €450M convertible; net financial assets €467M (YE2025 cash+STI €225M, then debt-free): still 4-6 quarters of runway, now with a convertible overlay.

## Industry Context

The MOCVD equipment industry is structurally a duopoly between Aixtron (Germany) and Veeco (US), with a long tail of smaller players (CCS Equipment, Tokuyama, Atomate, NIPPON SANSO) addressing specific subsegments. Total MOCVD equipment TAM is approximately $1.0-1.2B globally in 2025, and is projected to reach $1.8-2.2B by 2028 driven by three converging cycles:

1. **InP photonics 6-inch transition** (~$300-400M cumulative equipment spend 2026-2028): The InP industry is shifting from 3-4 inch wafers to 6-inch. [[Theses/LITE - Lumentum]] Greensboro is the canonical reference fab; Coherent (Sherman, Allen TX), Nokia (Espoo), SMART Photonics (Eindhoven), II-VI Saxony, and IQE epi-foundry are all building or expanding 6-inch InP capacity. This wave is concentrated 2026-2028 with capacity feeding 2028-2030 photonics revenue.

2. **Data-center 800V power** (~$200-300M cumulative 2026-2028): NVIDIA's 800V transition is the dominant demand pull, but the broader migration of AI rack power architectures from 48V/54V to 400V/800V layers ~2-3x GaN-on-Si epi requirement on top of consumer/auto demand. Tier-1 power management chip makers (Vicor, Delta Electronics, Innoscience, Navitas) are the indirect customer base; their fab partners (TSMC, GlobalFoundries 200mm, Innoscience captive) are the direct equipment buyers. The full six-layer value chain (grid/MV → SST → DC distribution → wide-bandgap silicon → VPD → passives) and adoption forecast (10-15% of new AI racks at 800VDC by 2027, 65-75% by 2032) is mapped in [[Macro & Technology/800VDC Adoption]]: AIXA's GaN-on-Si epi-tools sit at the wide-bandgap-silicon layer, which is the only layer where capacity-cycle lead times (12-18 months) exceed the 800VDC ramp window, making epi-tool order pull a leading indicator of mid-2027 rack-volume realization.

3. **SiC power normalization + India/Eastern Europe buildout** (~$300-400M cumulative 2026-2028): SiC is past peak hype but normalized at meaningful baseline: Wolfspeed restructuring, ROHM's India $700M fab, ON Semi Czech expansion, plus Chinese internal SiC capacity all drive 200mm SiC MOCVD tool demand at lower growth but durable absolute levels.

Competitive dynamics:

- **Aixtron** (~24% headline MOCVD share, ~70%+ InP-specific share, ~90%+ 6-inch InP G10-AsP share): differentiated on the high-margin InP/photonics segment, exposed in SiC/GaN power (more commodity-like). Strategic emphasis since 2022 has been doubling down on photonics: G10-AsP development, 6-inch reactor architecture, recipe library expansion to laser-specific structures.

- **Veeco** (~28% headline MOCVD share, ~9-12% Compound Semi revenue share within Veeco itself): weighted toward mature LED MOCVD (legacy installed base) and 200mm SiC competing with Aixtron G10-SiC. Less exposed to the 6-inch InP transition: Propel 6-inch InP is on Veeco's roadmap but not shipping at competitive scale as of FY2025. Veeco's CEO commentary on the FY2025 call framed compound semi as "9% to 12% growth into 2026", directionally consistent with secular but not transformational for Veeco's overall mix.

- **Long tail (CCS, Tokuyama, Atomate, NIPPON SANSO)**: regional / niche players, not credible threats in 6-inch InP or 200mm SiC at scale. Some lab-scale and R&D positions but not high-volume fab-scale equipment.

The value chain from precursors to end products positions Aixtron as the bottleneck:

```
Wafer substrate (SUMCO, Shin-Etsu, Coherent InP wafers)
  → Aixtron MOCVD epi tool (epitaxial growth)
    → Compound semi fab (Lumentum, Coherent, IQE epi-foundry)
      → Device fab (Lumentum laser fab, Coherent EML fab)
        → Module/transceiver maker (Marvell, Ciena, Innolight)
          → Hyperscaler / network OEM (AWS, Microsoft, Cisco, Nokia)
```

Aixtron sits at the second-most-leveraged position in this chain (behind only the wafer suppliers). The leverage manifests as: capacity expansion downstream requires Aixtron's tools 18-24 months ahead of revenue, so AIXA orders are the leading indicator for 2027-2028 photonics revenue at LITE/COHR.

### MOCVD physics, InP specialization, and AIXA's moat against new entrants

MOCVD (Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition) is epitaxy: ultrapure metal-organic precursor gases (TMGa, TMIn) and hydrides (PH₃, AsH₃, NH₃) are introduced into a 500-1,600°C reactor, undergo pyrolysis, and deposit one atomic layer per pass onto a wafer substrate. Growth is deliberately slow (2-5 hours per run) because deposited atoms must align to the substrate's lattice within sub-Angstrom tolerance; sub-nanometer mismatch propagates as crystal defects that destroy device yield. A single laser or HEMT device stacks 30-200+ layers, each <10 nm to several microns, with different thermal expansion coefficients; the operator must compensate for thermal stresses that bow and crack the wafer at scale. This inverts CMOS plain-silicon manufacturing: for digital logic, lithography is the constraint and the wafer is easy; for compound semis, deposition itself is the bottleneck.

**InP/AsP epitaxy is the hardest MOCVD variant**. Phosphorus is volatile (PH₃ cracks easily, contaminates chambers, requires higher overpressure than AsH₃ or NH₃); lattice and thermal mismatches with practical substrates capped historical wafer sizes at 3-4 inches; 6-inch is happening now and is non-trivial; 8-inch remains research-stage. The G10-AsP is purpose-built for As/P chemistry: distinct precursor injection geometry, chamber materials, and process-control loops from G10-GaN or G10-SiC. A photonics customer cannot run InP recipes on a GaN tool; conversion is not economically attractive. This is the structural reason the InP installed base is a separate market from GaN/SiC despite all three being MOCVD.

**Competitive comparison: what's actually shipping in the InP segment**:

| Player | Tool | Wafer size | Status vs. AIXA G10-AsP |
|---|---|---|---|
| **AIXA** | G10-AsP | 6-inch (150mm) InP/AsP | Tool of record; multi-customer qualification |
| Veeco | Propel (InP variant) | 4-inch primarily | Single-wafer architecture; not at 6-inch competitive scale; Q4-2024 €28M Epiluvac/NuFlare impairment after 2-year delay |
| ASMI | LPE (acquired €430M, 2022) | 4-6 inch SiC primarily | Single-wafer disadvantaged on TCO; SiC-focused, limited InP traction |
| TEL | Probus (single-wafer SiC) | 6-inch SiC | "Considered a failed system" per former SiC executive at major Western power semi; not in InP |
| AMAT | (Tried 2005, 2010) | — | Withdrew both attempts; no commercial MOCVD traction |
| AMEC (China) | Prismo | Mixed | Commodity LED only: declined from 55% of AMEC revenue (2017) to 7% (2023); pivoted to etch |
| NuFlare (Toshiba) | — | — | "Generally poor reviews" per industry research |
| Other deposition (PVD, ALD, plain CVD) | — | — | Cannot grow multi-micron III-V epitaxial stacks; physically inadequate substitute |

PVD (sputtering) is non-epitaxial and lattice-incoherent; ALD deposits sub-nanometer films but cannot do micron-scale III-V stacks; plain CVD without metal-organic precursors lacks precursor purity for compound device-grade epitaxy. For photonics-grade InP devices, MOCVD is the only economically viable process; the across-deposition-type comparison is moot.

**AIXA's moat against deposition-savvy new entrants: six layers**:

1. **Multi-wafer planetary reactor IP** (25+ years of refinement). AIXA's planetary tool processes 5×200mm or 9×150mm wafers per batch with single-wafer uniformity. Veeco TurboDisc relies on high-rotation single-wafer architecture; the Veeco VP of Technology himself acknowledged in industry interview that *"the high speed of rotation can actually introduce some mechanical stress on the wafer and lead to wafer defects, nonuniformity, thermal issues and so forth that makes it much more challenging to deliver the same level of epi performance that the Aixtron tool has."* Veeco's 300mm GaN tool is forced to single-wafer showerhead, sacrificing throughput. The planetary moat is process know-how, not patentable; competitors cannot copy by inspection.
2. **In-situ cleaning** (G10 family). Integrated reactor self-cleaning between runs. Competitor tools require manual offline cleaning, a yield-loss risk and TCO disadvantage. Asian SiC fabs achieving 99% yield on AIXA tools where comparable Chinese fabs run 50% historic yields on alternative tools.
3. **Process control depth**. Spectroscopic ellipsometry (layer thickness), reflectometry (growth rate), and deflectometry (wafer stress) integrated as in-situ feedback loops. The recipe library accumulated since 1983, thousands of customer-tuned process windows for specific device types, is the highest-value IP. A new entrant copying an AIXA tool would still need 5-10 years of customer co-development to match production-grade recipes.
4. **Customer switching cost**. Per the Veeco VP of Technology interview itself: *"You find that a company invests in a platform; it's everything from spares, layout of the fab, training of the teams. The operators, the scientists that run the tool, they get to understand their equipment very well. Shifting to a different platform really changes all of those factors... how you specifically achieve the optimal results on the system is quite different between the [Veeco and Aixtron] platforms. That does represent a barrier to entry."* Switching costs to displace an installed AIXA tool exceed the marginal cost of adding capacity on a new AIXA tool.
5. **Wafer-size leadership lock-in**. AIXA was first to 200mm GaN (2024 Infineon ramp), first to 6-inch InP (G10-AsP). Each migration to a larger wafer renders smaller-wafer competitors uncompetitive on TCO; customers scrap 150mm in favor of 200mm rather than retrofit. Pushing the wafer-size frontier is the structural mechanism that prevents competitor catch-up.
6. **China localization risk is bounded for InP specifically**. Domestic Chinese MOCVD attempts (Naura, AMEC, 3SBio) have succeeded in commodity LED but failed in advanced GaN-on-Si, 200mm SiC, and InP. Aixtron has never had a tool reverse-engineered in China; the planetary multi-wafer design requires 20+ years of process IP plus access to high-quality Western gas-delivery and process-control modules. For 6-inch InP specifically, the chemistry is harder than SiC (which Chinese players have struggled with), and the customer base is largely ex-China (Lumentum, Coherent, Nokia, SMART Photonics).

**Net moat assessment**: AIXA's monopoly economics in 6-inch InP MOCVD persist for ~2-3 years (2026-2028) on process know-how + planetary reactor IP + customer integration depth. AIXA's moat is a 5-10 year window before a determined, well-capitalized competitor (Veeco at 300mm GaN, possibly a future Chinese entrant) could ship a competitive 6-inch InP product, and is not equivalent to ASML's EUV monopoly (physically irreproducible). Outside that window, AIXA retains share leadership through scale economics + recipe library lock-in but with shared-vendor pricing dynamics. Thesis monopoly economics are 2-3 years; structural share leadership extends through 2030+.

Pricing power in InP MOCVD has expanded materially in 2024-2026: G10-AsP ASPs estimated to have risen ~15-25% in this period through tool feature richness (in-situ metrology integration, multi-wafer carrier upgrades) plus genuine pricing power in a single-vendor segment. This contrasts with the 2018-2022 LED MOCVD cycle where ASP compression was severe (China LED overcapacity drove tool ASPs down 30%+). The current InP cycle has structurally tighter customer concentration (single-digit customers vs. dozens of LED fabs) which historically supports better pricing discipline.

### Why Lam Research and Applied Materials stay out of MOCVD

AIXA is not protected by out-resourcing the WFE giants; the protection runs the other way. AMAT (~$27B revenue, ~$3.2B annual R&D) and LRCX (~$16B revenue, ~$1.9B annual R&D) each spend more on R&D in a single year than the entire global MOCVD equipment TAM (~$1.0-1.2B in 2025, ~$1.8-2.2B by 2028). The niche survives because it is simultaneously too small to move their needle and too know-how-intensive to enter quickly. Four barriers compound:

| Barrier | Why it deters AMAT / LRCX |
|---|---|
| **TAM immateriality** | 100% of MOCVD ≈ 4% of AMAT revenue / ~7% of LRCX revenue. Realistic share against a 25-40-year incumbent duopoly, won over 5+ years, is a rounding error. The marginal R&D dollar earns far more in gate-all-around transistors, backside power delivery, HBM/DRAM (where deposition and etch intensity is climbing fastest), and advanced packaging, each a $1B+ incremental TAM inside their existing 300mm silicon customer base. |
| **Process-DNA mismatch** | AMAT/LRCX core IP is deposition and etch on silicon (PVD, plasma/thermal CVD, ALD, CMP, etch): fast (minutes per wafer), single-wafer, 300mm-volume, depositing amorphous/polycrystalline films or removing material. MOCVD is slow (2-5 hours), batch/planetary, single-crystal III-V heteroepitaxy with toxic metal-organic precursors. Even AMAT's silicon-epi franchise (Centura/Epi, reduced-pressure CVD) is homoepitaxy on Si; the lattice-matching, precursor chemistry, and reactor architecture do not carry over. "Deposition know-how" is not fungible across this boundary. |
| **Recipe-library moat is unbuyable** | The asset is 25-40 years of customer-tuned process recipes plus planetary multi-wafer reactor IP (AIXA shipping since 1983). A new entrant needs 5-10 years of customer co-development to reach production-grade yield. AMAT cannot acquire the shortcut: the only targets are the duopoly itself (AIXA, Veeco), and bolt-on deals deliver neither the planetary architecture nor the recipe corpus. |
| **Customer-structure mismatch** | AMAT/LRCX go-to-market is built for a broad base of high-volume silicon fabs (TSMC, Samsung, Intel, Micron, SK Hynix) ordering hundreds of tools on predictable WFE cycles. MOCVD is single-digit compound-semi customers, lumpy orders, and brutal cyclicality: China LED overcapacity cut tool ASPs 30%+ in 2018-2022. The niche does not fit a $27B operating model or service footprint. |

**Revealed preference is the decisive evidence**: AMAT entered MOCVD twice (2005, 2010) and exited both times. The best-capitalized, deepest-deposition WFE player on earth tried, with the balance sheet to brute-force it, and withdrew. The barrier was never capital; it was the multi-year recipe and yield grind against entrenched incumbents in a market too small to justify the climb.

This is disruption-immunity through small-TAM specialization, the inverse of the Christensen pattern. AIXA is shielded precisely because the segment is too small to attract the giants and too specialized for a fast entry, the structural profile of a durable niche-equipment monopoly (the same setup re-rating [[Theses/BESI - BE Semiconductor Industries]] in hybrid bonding). The practical thesis implication: the credible threats to AIXA's moat stay Veeco (a focused peer already inside the niche and willing to grind the curve) and a state-subsidized Chinese entrant (where industrial policy overrides the TAM and ROIC math), not the WFE incumbents. AMAT/LRCX entry is the lowest-probability path to moat erosion, which is why §Outstanding Questions frames the moat-window debate around Veeco and China, not the deposition giants.

## Management and culture

Hypothesis: Inert on [[Lens - Management and Culture]]: Gate 1 passes (SiC/GaN/InP/photonics tool optionalities); Gate 2 fails because the photonics pipeline is already in the multiple and the sell-side narrative (NTM ~55x trough FY26, Kerrisdale public Nov-2025, H1 2026 opto 54% of equipment revenue). Grade the name on other models. [MC-2] 2025 Vergütungsbericht: two-person Vorstand (Grawert CEO since Mar-2021, contract to Aug-2030); LTI 50% relative TSR / 35% net profit / 15% ESG from 2025 (TSR weight raised from 40%); STI 70% net profit with no ROIC or product-volume metric; 1×-base ownership guideline; one-share-one-vote SE, no founder control; open-market buys 27-Feb-2025 Grawert €66k at €11.84 and Danninger €69k at €12.36, SB deputy van Hout €114k 31-Oct-2025, all predate the 2026 rally. [MC-7] headcount 1,207 YE2024 → 1,035 mid-2026, product/functional org far below the ~5,000 ceiling. [MC-6]/[G-10] entropy and new-venture-destruction base rates are not the live constraint while Gate 2 is closed.

## Bull Case

Base bull case (12-18 month horizon, 40-60% upside):

**Operating mix-shift continues at observed pace**: Q1 2026 65% optoelectronics order share holds or expands through Q2-Q4. FY2026 actuals print revenue €580-620M (above current €560M guide midpoint), 50%+ optoelectronics revenue mix exiting 2026, EBIT margin 19-21% (modest recovery from FY2025 18%). FY2027 consensus revenue revisions follow: current ~€690M consensus → €750-800M revised consensus by Q4 2026. EPS revisions of +20-30% on current 2027 numbers.

**Multiple re-rating from semis-equipment to photonics-equipment band**: Current ~32x forward P/E reflects SiC/GaN power equipment cycle mid-multiple. As InP/photonics revenue exceeds 50% of mix and demonstrates durable order book through 2027-2028, the comp set shifts from VECO (~22x) to ASMI (~32x) toward BESI (~38x). Re-rating to 40x forward P/E on revised €4.50 FY2027 EPS (vs current ~€3.20 consensus) implies ~€180/share, well above current ~€21. (Note: AIXA has had a significant rally; absolute share-price targets here are illustrative of multiple expansion logic, not point estimates.)

**Second leg materializes: 800V data-center GaN orders land in 2H 2026**: NVIDIA 800V transition order signaling lands at GTC 2026 or fall 2026 supplier earnings, AIXA captures GaN-on-Si epi capacity orders for 2027-2028 NVIDIA Rubin/Rubin-Ultra rack shipments. Adds €100-200M cumulative incremental order book over 2H 2026 - 1H 2027, providing a second independent revenue S-curve through 2028. Adoption-curve framework anchoring this second leg in [[Macro & Technology/800VDC Adoption]] (base case: 10-15% of new AI racks at 800VDC by 2027 → 65-75% by 2032): at the early-adopter inflection point, GaN-on-Si epi capacity becomes the binding constraint because OCP Mt. Diablo sidecar adoption (Meta/Google co-authored) parallels NVIDIA's Kyber spec, doubling the demand surface across both 800VDC paths.

**Stretch bull (Kerrisdale-style)**: G10-AsP 6-inch InP monopoly persists through 2028 with no credible Veeco competitive product, NVIDIA 800V layers on as 2027-2028 second leg, FY2029 revenue reaches €1.4B with EBIT margins expanding to 25-30% on operating leverage. EPS €2 in 2028, €3+ in 2029. At a 35-40x multiple on €3 EPS, share price ~€110-120. This is the Kerrisdale Capital scenario; achievement requires multiple non-trivial conditions to hold, but each individually has plausible mechanism support.

### Kerrisdale Capital long thesis (November 2025) — full summary

Kerrisdale published "AIXTRON SE (GR:AIXA): The Next AI and Datacenter Play" in November 2025 at €13.88/share (€1,565M market cap, AIXA had collapsed -44% over the prior 3 years vs +217% for peer average). Headline output: €55.01/share fair value (avg of two methodologies), **+296% upside**. Three pillars below.

**Pillar 1: "ASML of compound semiconductor deposition" (technology and market-share leadership)**:

- Aggregate MOCVD share: ~70%. Segment-level: 90%+ in GaN power MOCVD (G10-GaN, ASP €4.0M); 90%+ in optoelectronics (G10-AsP for InP/GaAs lasers, ASP €3.5M); top-2 player at 35-40% in SiC (G10-SiC ASP €4.5M, winning 50-60% of new business in 200mm transition); top-2 in red/orange/yellow LED (G5+C, ASP €3.0M).
- Differentiated technology: planetary batch reactor design (5-9 wafers per run vs single-wafer competitors), in-situ cleaning capability, recipe library accumulated since 1983, aggressive wafer-size leadership (200mm GaN with Infineon 2024, 200mm SiC dominant in China, 150mm InP via G10-AsP).
- Competitive position: Veeco "failed to invest in Propel": Q4-2024 €28M impairment of Epiluvac/NuFlare technology, 2-year delay vs. AIXA. AMEC pivoted away from MOCVD (declined from 55% of revenue in 2017 to 7% in 2023). TEL Probus single-wafer SiC tool "considered a failed system" per former SiC executive at major Western power semi. ASMI acquired LPE for €430M (2022) but disadvantaged by single-wafer TCO. AMAT tried MOCVD twice (2005, 2010) and failed both times.
- Customer base: Western power semis (Infineon, STMicro, ON Semiconductor, Texas Instruments), lasers (Coherent, Lumentum, Broadcom, Trumpf, Furukawa), LEDs (ams-OSRAM, LumiLEDs, LG Innotek, Samsung), Chinese players (SiCC, Innoscience, Sanan Optoelectronics). All 14 power semi suppliers in NVIDIA's 800V ecosystem are AIXA customers.

**Pillar 2: Critical AI/data-center demand drivers**:

*GaN power: NVIDIA 800V HVDC*. IEA forecasts data-center electricity to double to 945 TWh by 2030. NVIDIA's 800V architecture (begins ramp 2027) replaces 48V/54V in-rack systems: 13.8kV grid → 800V at perimeter (SiC) → point-of-load (GaN) for 1MW+ racks. Yole forecasts GaN power market $355M (2024) → $2.9B (2030); TrendForce $390M → $3.5B (44% CAGR). Navitas sized 800V data-center power opportunity (GaN+SiC) at $2.6B with GaN dominant. AIXA expects orders to commence late 2026 / ramp throughout 2027. Infineon plans 30,000 wafers/month at 300mm GaN; Innoscience targets 70,000 wafers/month by 2027. Veeco's Morgan Stanley conference comment sized the Infineon GaN opportunity alone at over 100 reactors × ~€4M ASP = ~€200M revenue from one customer.

*SiC power: durable second leg*. Yole forecasts SiC device market $3.2B (2023) → $10.3B (2030, 20% CAGR). Wolfspeed estimates 200mm enables ~80% increase in die per wafer and could reduce device costs 54% by 2030. AIXA management: all China SiC business is now 200mm; Chinese customers scrapping 150mm tools. AIXA sold its 100th SiC system; share moving from 37% (Yole 2023) to 50-60% in 200mm China opportunities. STMicro's Catania 200mm ramp could generate >€750M in MOCVD tool orders.

*Optoelectronics: AI bandwidth wave*. AIXA dominant tool (~90% share) for laser InP/GaAs epitaxy. Industry migrating to 150mm InP wafers; G10-AsP qualified at every major laser supplier. Coherent tripled InP capacity for 800G ramp; estimates pluggable optics market at $25B by 2030. PIC market $5B → $40B by 2035 (IDTechEx). AIXA expects optoelectronics 50%+ YoY growth in 2H 2025 and 25-30% in 2026.

Kerrisdale models 47% gross margin and 28% EBITDA margin in 2028 (vs Aixtron's last 52.5% gross margin in 2010 at ~€800M scale). Cash flow: ~€280M FCF generation 2H 2025 through 2026; €250-300M target cash balance by year-end 2026; capex normalized to €29-32M/year (post €100M Innovation Center buildout in 2024).

Two valuation methodologies:

1. **Discounted P/E off 2028E EPS**: Apply small-cap peer median 33.5x P/E to Kerrisdale 2028E EPS of €1.90 → implied 2027 stock price €63.53 → discount back two years at 11.1% WACC → **€51.50 today, +271% upside**.
2. **DCF**: 11.1% WACC, 25x EV/LTM EBITDA exit multiple. Yields **€58.53 fair value, +322% upside**. Terminal value €14,666M; PV of terminal €5,135M; PV of cash flows €1,313M; net cash €153M; equity value €6,601M / 112.8M shares.

Average: **€55.01, +296% upside** from Nov-2025 €13.88.

**Counter-arguments addressed in the report**:
- Chinese localization: AIXA "about as insulated as possible": Chinese MOCVD attempts have failed in advanced applications; Chinese customers actively scrap 150mm and buy AIXA 200mm tools.
- Veeco/competitive risk: Veeco failed to invest in Propel; AMEC pivoted to etch; ASMI/TEL disadvantaged by single-wafer architecture; AMAT failed twice (2005, 2010).
- Cyclical concerns: 2013-2016 EBITDA margins ranged -4% to -37% on €193M revenue; current LTM 22% EBITDA on €596M revenue is structurally improved diversification profile.
- Multiple compression: AIXA underperformed -44% vs +217% peer average over 3 years; multiple compressed 51% since 2024, setting up the "powerful re-rating" thesis catalyst.

**Risks flagged by Kerrisdale**:
- Single-quarter results could continue to compress shares ("we'd rather be early than late").
- Power demand softness could persist through 2026 before 2027 reacceleration.
- MicroLED timing remains uncertain (Apple's Feb-2024 delay sent AIXA -20%).
- AIXA was at "20-year low price/tangible book ratio" near publication.

**Implications for current (Apr 30 2026) AIXA thesis**: AIXA's +138% YTD rally has closed roughly half the discount Kerrisdale identified: current ~32x forward P/E is closer to the small-cap peer 33.5x median than the 19.6x at Kerrisdale's analysis point. However, Kerrisdale's 2027E/2028E revenue (€735M / €1,060M) remains materially above current Bloomberg consensus (€690M / ~€775M). If Q1 2026 results validate optoelectronics mix-shift trajectory, sell-side EPS revisions toward Kerrisdale's €1.90 2028E figure provide an additional 30-50% upside on top of multiple-driven re-rating already realized, directly supporting the Stretch bull scenario above.

What has to go right (rank-ordered by probability):
1. Q1 2026 -38% EBIT margin reverses by Q2-Q3 as revenue recognition catches up to order intake. (~75-85% probability based on quarterly seasonality history)
2. FY2026 €560M guide is met or modestly exceeded. (~70% probability based on order-book coverage)
3. Optoelectronics share of mix continues to expand quarterly through 2026. (~65-75% probability based on customer disclosure trajectory)
4. NVIDIA 800V second leg materializes in 2H 2026 / 1H 2027. (~50-60% probability: single-customer dependency)
5. Multiple re-rates from ~32x to ~40x by mid-2027. (~50% probability: depends on market narrative shift)
6. Veeco / Asian competitor does not ship competitive 6-inch InP MOCVD before 2028. (~75% probability: process know-how moat is real but not impenetrable)

## Bear Case

Base bear case (12-18 month horizon, 30-50% downside):

**Q1 2026 -38% EBIT margin signals customer push-out, not seasonality**: Apr 30 results call discloses that Q2 backlog conversion is below historical run-rate, and FY2026 €560M guide is at risk by 5-10%. Stock prices a guide cut at the next print (Q2 results in late July). H1 cash flow turns materially negative, raising questions about FY2026 free cash flow. Multiple compresses from ~32x to ~22-25x on guide cut and execution doubt.

**The +138% YTD rally has already absorbed the mix-shift narrative**: Kerrisdale Capital's long thesis is in the public domain since early 2026 and has been actively traded. Sell-side EPS revisions to 2027 numbers have been moderate (~5-10% upward) but the share price has run +138%, implying multiple expansion has done most of the work, leaving downside asymmetric on any execution disappointment. Mean-reversion in the multiple back to 25-28x on flat EPS revisions implies ~25-30% downside before fundamental concerns.

**Veeco ships competitive 6-inch InP MOCVD by 2H 2027**: Veeco's R&D priority on Compound Semiconductor is real, and the technical gap on a 6-inch InP-equivalent product is process know-how, not a fundamentally different physics. If Veeco ships a competitive Propel 6-inch InP variant by 2H 2027, possibly 2-3 years ahead of base-case bear timing, Aixtron's vendor monoculture window collapses to <1 year, pricing pressure on G10-AsP ASPs follows, and gross margin trajectory inflects from "expanding to 45%+" to "reverting to 38-40%."

**NVIDIA 800V slips to 2028 or 2029**: Rubin/Rubin-Ultra schedule slip pushes the data-center 800V GaN demand wave from 2H 2026 - 1H 2027 to 2H 2027 - 2H 2028, removing the second-leg revenue support that the 2027 numbers depend on. Combined with photonics order book digestion (typical 18-24 month equipment-to-revenue lag means 2027 will absorb a digestion period after the 2026 order intake spike), 2027 revenue growth slows materially or turns flat.

**Stretch bear (downside scenario, 12-24 month)**: All four conditions occur: Q2 guide cut, multiple compression, Veeco ships competitor, NVIDIA slips. FY2027 revenue lands €600-650M (vs current €690M consensus), EBIT margin 15-18% (vs 22-25% bull case), EPS €2.30-2.60 (vs current ~€3.20 consensus). Multiple compresses to 22x on €2.50 EPS = ~€55/share, implying 30-50% downside from current levels. This is a low-probability scenario (~15-20%) but not far-fetched given how much the rally has already priced in.

What does the world look like where AIXA loses money:
- InP photonics 6-inch transition disappoints due to data-center optical capex pause (e.g., AI capex cycle 2027 trough), customers cut Greensboro/Sherman/Espoo capacity 30-50%, AIXA's 2027-2028 order book collapses by ~€150-200M.
- Concurrently, China subsidizes a domestic InP MOCVD competitor (Aixtron-China, Naura, 3SBio MOCVD) that takes 30%+ of the China-domestic InP capacity orders by 2028.
- SiC/GaN power demand doesn't recover materially: EV growth disappoints in Europe and US, China capacity keeps prices low globally, and SiC equipment ASPs compress 15-25%.
- The +138% YTD rally fully reverses; multiple compression to 18-22x on suppressed €2 EPS prints = €40-45/share, ~50% downside.

## Catalysts

**Apr 30 2026: Q1 2026 earnings call (immediate, near-term high-stakes)**: Confirmation of preliminary €171M order intake, application split breakdown for Q1 orders, FY2026 guide reaffirmation or revision, gross margin trajectory commentary, customer concentration disclosure. This is the single most important near-term datapoint for the thesis. A reaffirmed FY guide + 65%+ optoelectronics order share + improving Q2 backlog visibility validates the mix-shift thesis. A guide cut or Q2 backlog softness rapidly reverses the bull narrative.

**Q2 2026 results (late July 2026)**: Mid-year operating leverage check: does the high fixed-cost base absorb Q2 revenue at 18-20% EBIT margin as expected? Is H1 free cash flow positive? Q2-end cash position. Strong Q2 + raised FY guide is the cleanest validation of the thesis; weak Q2 + unchanged guide implies H2 has to deliver more than base case.

**June 2026: NVIDIA GTC + Computex disclosures**: NVIDIA Rubin/Rubin-Ultra schedule commentary, 800V power supplier roadmap, hyperscaler 1.6T optical transceiver volume guidance from Marvell/Innolight/Lumentum. These shape the 2027 demand assumptions for AIXA's second-leg (800V) and durability for the first-leg (photonics).

**Q3 2026 results (late October 2026)**: Order book composition disclosure (InP vs SiC vs GaN-power split) for Q3 backlog. By Q3 2026, the 2027 revenue will be nearly fully booked given 12-18 month equipment lead times; Q3 results will be the leading read on 2027 revenue trajectory.

**FY2026 results (early February 2027)**: Full-year mix shift validation. Optoelectronics share of equipment revenue >35-40% would confirm the thesis trajectory; <30% would suggest the mix shift has stalled or reversed.

**Veeco FY2026 results (Feb 2027) and Compound Semi guidance for FY2027**: Direct read on competitive intensity. Veeco compound semi guide of 15-20% growth (vs 12% FY2026 starting point) signals equipment market demand stronger than expected; Veeco compound semi guide of <10% growth signals market consolidation toward AIXA in InP specifically.

**Q1 2027 announcements / late 2026 Veeco product disclosures (potential bearish catalyst)**: First credible signal of Veeco 6-inch InP MOCVD shipping product would be a major thesis input. Look for Veeco Propel platform updates at SEMICON West (July 2026), CS Mantech (May 2026), or earnings call commentary.

## Risks

Thesis risks (the investment case is wrong):

**InP photonics demand peaks earlier than modeled**: The current photonics order wave is driven by hyperscaler 1.6T transceiver buildout for 2027-2028 deployments. If the AI capex cycle troughs in 2027 or hyperscaler 1.6T deployment slips, customers (LITE, COHR, Nokia) push out 6-inch capacity buildout, and AIXA's 2027-2028 order book trajectory inflects down. This is the dominant thesis risk.

**Veeco competitive 6-inch InP MOCVD product ships before 2028**: Aixtron's monopoly window in 6-inch InP G10-AsP is the foundation of pricing power and gross margin expansion in the bull case. A Veeco competitive product compresses ASPs and gross margins by 15-25% within 4-6 quarters of competitive launch, even if AIXA retains majority share.

**Sector-domestic Chinese MOCVD entrant gains material InP share**: China's Naura, 3SBio MOCVD, or a captive at SMIC/CXMT-equivalent foundry could ship 6-inch InP MOCVD at ~70% of Western pricing as part of the broader semiconductor independence push. This is currently low-probability for high-volume 6-inch InP (the chemistry is harder than SiC) but is a real tail risk for 2028+ orders.

**Operating leverage fails to materialize on revenue ramp**: Aixtron's high fixed-cost base (€135M annual) means EBIT margin expansion requires meaningful revenue growth. If FY2027 revenue lands €650M vs current ~€788M consensus, EBIT margin expansion stalls at 20% rather than rising to 22-25%, and EPS leverage to revenue is muted.

Position risks (thesis is right but stock goes down anyway):

**Multiple compression on broader semis cyclicality**: AIXA trades in correlation with the broader semis equipment complex (SOX index, ASMI, BESI, AMAT). A semis-equipment cycle drawdown in 2027 driven by macro slowdown or AI capex pause compresses AIXA's multiple regardless of company-specific execution. Beta to SOX is approximately 1.3-1.5 historically.

**The +138% YTD rally has crowded the long side**: Hedge fund positioning data (limited disclosure for a German mid-cap, but Kerrisdale-style long thesis published indicates active long positioning) suggests the easy gains have been collected. A position-unwind event (e.g., margin call cascade, factor rotation away from photonics names) could compress the multiple even on operationally clean execution.

**EUR/USD currency exposure**: Aixtron reports in EUR, sells globally with significant USD exposure (US customers + Asian customers often pricing in USD), and bears EUR cost base. A USD weakening cycle in 2026-2027 erodes reported revenue and margin growth optically.

**Single-customer concentration**: Disclosure suggests 5-7 InP customers account for the vast majority of optoelectronics revenue. Push-out at any 1-2 of these (Lumentum Greensboro phase 2, Coherent Sherman, Nokia Espoo expansion) is enough to materially impact the order book.

## Conviction Triggers

→ **HIGH if**: Q1 2026 earnings (Apr 30) confirms ≥60% optoelectronics order share, FY2026 €560M guide is reaffirmed or raised, AND Q3 2026 results disclose ≥40% optoelectronics share of equipment revenue with EBIT margin tracking ≥20%. The combination validates the mix-shift thesis as durable, not a one-quarter spike, with operating leverage materializing as the revenue base normalizes.

→ **LOW if**: Q1 2026 earnings disclose Q2 backlog conversion below 80% of normal seasonal pace, OR FY2026 guide is cut by ≥5%, OR Veeco announces a 6-inch InP MOCVD product with named first customer at any 2026 event (CS Mantech May, SEMICON West July, Veeco earnings). Any of these signals the thesis economics are eroding faster than base case.

→ **CLOSE if**: FY2026 actual results (Feb 2027) print optoelectronics share <30% of equipment revenue AND FY2027 guide is below current €690M consensus by ≥10%, OR Veeco ships competitive 6-inch InP MOCVD with multiple confirmed customers by Q3 2027. Either signals the structural thesis (InP monopoly + accelerating mix shift) has failed to materialize, with no second-leg story strong enough to compensate.
