## Bull Case
- **Physical AI becomes a multi-trillion-dollar market; Nvidia owns the full stack from training → simulation → edge inference.** No competitor spans all three compute environments. ABB, FANUC, KUKA, Yaskawa (2M+ installed robots) already integrating Nvidia silicon and software.
- **Software margins expand as Omniverse Enterprise, Cosmos platform licensing, and sovereign AI contracts scale.** The transition from hardware-only to hardware+software revenue structurally improves margin profile and revenue durability.
- **Sovereign AI creates government-backed demand floors across NATO nations and strategic partners.** $30B already, 3x YoY growth, insulated from corporate capex cycles. 20+ AI factories across Europe.
- **Hyperscaler capex cycle extends through 2028+ on agentic AI, Physical AI, and inference scaling demand.** Q1 FY2027 printed $81.6B (+85% YoY) vs the $78B guide; Q2 guided to $91B (street $93–95B). Top-4 CY2026 capex plans total ~$725B+ (+77% YoY): Microsoft Q2 $41B (+70%), Meta $42B, Alphabet raised to $195–205B, Amazon ~$220B. Every major cloud provider committed to Vera Rubin adoption.
- **Warp/PhysX performance gap widens with each hardware generation due to hardware-software co-optimization.** Annual cadence (Blackwell → Rubin → Feynman) creates compound advantage ASIC programs on 2–3 year cycles cannot match.
- **Open-source model proliferation increases infrastructure demand via Jevons Paradox.** The more AI becomes commoditized at the model layer, the more compute the ecosystem consumes in aggregate. Nvidia wins on volume regardless of which model company captures end-user revenue.
- **The Groq LPX licensing deal secures Nvidia's position in SRAM-based inference**, preventing a potential competitive blind spot from becoming a vulnerability while monetizing inference through licensing rather than silicon.
- **Valuation compressed from 45x+ (2024) to ~23x forward P/E at the July trough; the market has since re-rated it to ~25x**, still pricing sustained dominance rather than perfection, but the cheap-multiple leg of the case is partly spent after the +7% one-month move. Any acceleration in Physical AI deployment or sovereign AI contracts creates upside to estimates.
- **Software keeps closing the inference gap**: TileRT persistent-kernel decode (InferenceX) and Dynamo/MLPerf v6.0 gains show same silicon delivering multi-fold tok/s/user via software, reinforcing CUDA/system moat vs specialist inference ASICs ([[Research/2026-08-10 - NVDA TileRT Ultra-High Interactivity InferenceX - deep-dive]], [[Research/2026-08-05 - NVDA BEP Inference Specialists vs System Moat - deep-dive]]).

## Bear Case
- **Hyperscaler custom ASICs (Google TPU v7, Amazon Trainium, Microsoft Maia) mature enough to break GPU dominance for inference workloads.** TPU v7 at ~70% cost reduction, Trainium at 30–40% better price-performance. The two best frontier models already run majority inference on non-Nvidia hardware. ASIC growth at 44.6% CAGR outpaces GPU growth.
- **TSMC fabrication concentration (Taiwan Strait geopolitical risk) creates existential supply vulnerability.** A military conflict or severe natural disaster in Taiwan would cripple GPU production for 12–24+ months with no viable alternative foundry at scale.
- **Algorithmic efficiency (Muon, TurboQuant, quantization) reduces GPU demand per workload faster than workload proliferation.** Trillion-parameter models now run on Apple Silicon hardware. If local/edge compute achieves state-of-the-art inference, cloud GPU demand erodes.
- **Physical AI ROI disappoints near-term**: "ChatGPT moment for robotics" stalls due to regulatory hurdles, "physical hallucination" problems, slow enterprise deployment timelines. The TAM expansion narrative delays by years while valuation embeds it today.
- **China export revenue never materializes despite policy relaxation.** $4.5B charge already taken. Huawei Ascend roadmap (950PR shipping Q1 2026, 950DT Q4 2026, 960 in 2027, 970 in 2028) with in-house HBM and 750K-unit 2026 volume now provides a concrete domestic alternative: ByteDance $5.6B order proves enterprise willingness to migrate. Atlas 950DT SuperCluster (520K chips, 524 EFLOPS FP8, Q4 2026) targets hyperscaler-scale deployments. ~$50B addressable market increasingly likely permanently lost regardless of US policy.
- **Market share erosion accelerates from 75% toward 60%** as ASIC software ecosystems mature and AMD's ROCm improves. Revenue growth decelerates even with TAM expansion.
- **The Groq LPX deal signals that GPUs are structurally suboptimal for dedicated inference**: Nvidia cancelled Rubin CPX and licensed Groq's SRAM architecture instead. Jensen frames this as inference market segmentation (premium-priced, low-latency tokens for high-value use cases like software engineering copilots vs throughput-optimized batch inference) rather than GPU inferiority. But cancelling a planned inference silicon product in favor of third-party licensing validates that GPU architecture alone cannot serve all inference market segments.

## Risks
1. **TSMC concentration:** Single foundry dependency on geopolitically exposed Taiwan; no viable alternative at equivalent process node for 2+ years
2. **Custom ASIC competition:** Google TPU v7, Amazon Trainium, Microsoft Maia closing inference cost gap; ASIC software ecosystems improving faster than consensus expects
3. **Algorithmic efficiency overshoot:** Compound efficiency gains (Muon 35% + TurboQuant 6x + quantization) could eventually overwhelm Jevons Paradox, reducing aggregate GPU demand
4. **HBM supply constraints:** SK Hynix (~60% share); Samsung HBM4 golden yield ~80% (Aug 2026, from ~50%) eases the single-source risk and opens Rubin Ultra dual-sourcing; 16-Hi stack yields of ~44% still constrain production volume
5. **China export uncertainty:** $4.5B charge taken; H200 at 25% tariff/50% volume cap; China may reject imports; ~$50B market at risk. Domestic alternatives (Huawei Ascend) shipping at scale: 950PR Q1 2026 (750K units planned), in-house HBM, ByteDance $5.6B committed, full roadmap through 2028 (970 targeting 4 ZettaFLOPS FP4)
6. **Physical AI timeline risk:** If robotics/AV deployment is slower than the simulation layer suggests, the TAM thesis delays while valuation embeds it
7. **Inference architecture disruption:** Groq LPX deal signals GPUs may not be optimal for dedicated inference; SRAM-based and TPU-based architectures could capture inference revenue
8. **Valuation requires sustained execution:** ~25x forward P/E on ~$394B FY2027 consensus revenue (+82%) embeds a further ~43% ramp to ~$564B FY2028 consensus; any deceleration compresses the multiple sharply in a cyclical semiconductor industry
9. **Tariff/trade policy uncertainty:** Broader US trade policy volatility (145% China tariffs on other goods) could disrupt supply chains and customer purchasing behavior
10. **NVLink scale-up moat erosion via the SerDes plateau:** Per [[Research/2026-05-31 - CPO Scale-Up Inflection and Supply Chain - deep-dive]], NVLink's 11× scale-up bandwidth gain (NVLink 1.0→5.0) came almost entirely from 10× SerDes speed (20G→200G), not lane count, and SerDes is plateauing (224G was hard; true 448G uni-directional uncertain, Rubin resorts to a bi-directional workaround). Copper scale-up hits a ~2-meter reach wall capping world size to 1-2 racks. CPO removes that constraint and gives hyperscaler / AMD scale-up fabrics four independent bandwidth-scaling vectors (fiber × baud × modulation × WDM) versus copper's single grinding lever: a structural opening to close the NVLink gap later-decade. Partially offset by Nvidia's own scale-up CPO lead (Quantum-X 200G-MRM in production disproves the NRZ-only notion) and Kyber rack density (144 GPU packages). The risk is to NVLink's *durability* as the scale-up moat, not near-term positioning. Sharpening (2026-08-16): the hyperscaler ASIC fabrics (TPU ICI/OCS, Trainium) are already *latency*-competitive with NVLink [1×: SemiAnalysis] and contest the scale-up layer at pod scale (Ironwood 9,216-chip superpod) by trading per-link bandwidth for domain scale + reconfigurable routing, so NVLink's durable edge narrows to switched any-to-any bandwidth for *dynamic* (MoE/RL) communication, not a uniform lead (§Industry Context → ASIC rack catch-up). InferenceX Q3 CY2026 is the falsifier.
11. **Third-party AI infrastructure financing cycle**: Aug 2026 MOUs with Apollo/BlackRock/Blackstone/Brookfield/GS/KKR target >$500B third-party capital (optional ~$125B Nvidia backstop) ([[Research/2026-08-12 - NVDA - Nvidia 500B AI Infrastructure Financing Platforms - news]], [[Research/2026-08-11 - NVDA Superposition AI Factory Underwriting - deep-dive]]). Constructive for deployment velocity *if* underwriting standards hold; Stratechery/Damodaran frames map railway-style leverage and Situational Awareness blow-up as path-dependent ruin risks when conviction is funded with maximal leverage ([[Research/2026-08-12 - NVDA - Risky Business Stratechery AI Financing - news]], [[Research/2026-08-12 - NVDA AVGO MRVL NOW - Damodaran Situational Awareness Blow-up - news]]). Watch utilization, residual value, and non-CUDA inference offtake share.
    - *2026-08-15 Temple 8 inversion* ([[Research/2026-08-14 - LITE CRWV NBIS NVDA - Temple 8 Earnings Week 500B MOU - deep-dive]]): GPUs fail the toll-road / energy / CRE underwriting triad: useful life debated, residual value untested in a downcycle, cash-flow counterparties mostly unprofitable. The $500B is a design target, not a committed fund and not NVDA revenue; even full execution covers less than one year of ~$570B 2026 AI debt / ~$850B DC capex [1×: Temple 8]. Self-interest qualifier: the vendor promoting residual-value durability is the vendor whose ASP depends on lenders believing it. This is a *financing-layer* challenge rather than a CUDA/Omniverse challenge. NVDA has **no `## Conviction Triggers`** to touch-check.
    - *2026-08-15 TSPA ODM-money bottleneck* ([[Research/2026-08-14 - TSM NVDA - TSPA AI Servers Bottleneck Money - deep-dive]]): a fifth financing tranche sits on Foxconn–Quanta–Wistron–Wiwynn working capital + Taiwan bank *group concentration*. Consignment vs ODM-owned GPU is the swing: if ODMs buy GPUs, bank caps can gate shipment velocity of an already-allocated GPU. Challenges treating an order booked / CoWoS reserved as a delivered rack [1×: TSPA].

# [133/159] Theses/ONON - On Holding.md
**thesis · ticker: ONON · status: draft · conviction: medium · sector: Athletic Footwear & Apparel · date: 2026-07-15 · tags: thesis, consumer, footwear, ONON · source: '[[Research/2026-07-14 - ONON - On Holding Business Breakdown - deep-dive.md]] + On Q4/FY2025 (2026-03-03) and Q1 2026 (2026-05-12) results'**

## Summary

On has been re-priced from a hyper-growth compounder (~$54, ~30x forward earnings) to a decelerating premium sneaker brand (~$37, ~21-25x, near its 52-week low of $31.41), yet the business that produced the de-rating grew Q1 2026 net sales +26.4% constant-currency, expanded gross margin 430bps to 64.2%, and took share while every large peer stalled. The sell-off was an expectations reset, not a demand event: FY2026 guidance of "≥23% cc" implied CHF 3.44B against CHF 3.67B consensus, and a CHF 173M non-cash FX loss cut reported FY2025 net income 15.9% even as operating profitability hit records. The investable question is narrow and unresolved: whether a founder-controlled, debt-free brand compounding 23%+ at a 64% gross margin off a ~CHF 3B base is a justified outlier to the brutal footwear base rate, or the first step of a taste-cycle fade now dressed up as "de-risked." At ~3x EV/revenue and ~16x EBITDA the price no longer demands the bull case, which is what makes the name interesting after a 32% drawdown; the founders re-took the CEO seats and bought stock at $36.64 into that drawdown. Medium conviction: the operating momentum, margin, balance sheet, and owner alignment are real, but the durability data that would earn "high" (cohort retention, LTV/CAC) is not disclosed, and low switching costs plus intensifying competition leave the base-rate bear fully alive.

## Key Non-consensus Insights

- **The de-rating priced a fade the numbers have not delivered: consensus repriced a beat-and-raise compounder as a fade candidate on optics (guide-vs-estimate + FX), not on a demand miss.**
  - **Consensus:** On's explosive growth is structurally cooling toward the footwear base rate; a 23% guide from a brand that grew 30%+ is the first visible step down, so ~21-25x forward is still not cheap enough for the deceleration risk.
  - **Variant:** 23% is On's characteristic sandbag, not a ceiling: it beat and raised margin guidance in Q1 (26.4% cc, gross margin +430bps), hit its 2023 Investor Day 18% EBITDA target a full year early, and the stock fell on a consensus that had over-extrapolated to 30%+, not on any softening of underlying sell-through. The de-rate to ~3x EV/revenue / ~16x EBITDA created the entry into a business still compounding mid-20s% with rising margins.
  - **First confirming observable [2026-08]:** Q2 2026 print delivers >23% cc growth with gross margin held ≥64% and no inventory build → the "cooling" narrative is optics, not fundamentals.
  - **Falsifier:** two consecutive quarters of sub-20% cc growth absent a macro shock (ties to → LOW trigger): the fade is real and consensus was early, not wrong.

- **LightSpray is valued as a $310 marketing halo. The same process is an early-stage robotic, localizable manufacturing platform that directly hedges the tariff and FX drag now compressing the stock.**
  - **Consensus:** spray-on uppers are a PR stunt on a sub-1% halo racing shoe; On is structurally a Vietnam-sourced importer absorbing a 20% tariff ($70M in Q1 alone) with no manufacturing edge.
  - **Variant:** On just scaled LightSpray capacity 30-fold (Busan +32 robots vs. 4 in Zurich a year ago), and a near-zero-labor, near-zero-waste, one-piece automated process is the one credible path to nearshoring production toward demand, cutting labor, shipping, and tariff exposure while deepening the "Swiss engineering" brand story. This is the only place On owns a genuine process-technology lever rather than pure brand rent (held as a hypothesis to test, not a verdict; consumer/physical automation is the hardest, most bounded case per the Automation lens sector overlay).
  - **First confirming observable [2026-2027]:** a mass-market (not racing) model shipping on LightSpray at volume, with management disclosing a unit-cost or tariff/logistics benefit.
  - **Falsifier:** LightSpray stays confined to sub-1% halo volumes through 2027 with no mass rollout and no disclosed cost benefit → it is marketing, and the tariff/FX drag is unmitigated (ties to → LOW trigger on margin).

- **The market read the double CEO exit as instability; the founders re-took operational control and bought stock at the lows: an alignment upgrade, not a governance risk.**
  - **Consensus:** losing CEO Hoffmann (also CFO, 13 years) within a year of co-CEO Maurer's departure, plus a new CFO, signals strategic drift and shakes confidence in the next growth phase.
  - **Variant:** Allemann and Coppetti, who built On's premium-discipline culture and control >50% of votes on ~26% economic ownership, chose to step back into operating roles at the moment execution matters most, and each put ~$2.2M of personal capital in at $36.64 alongside co-founder Bernhard. Founder-led, founder-owned, founder-buying is the governance profile that beats the base rate; the market is discounting it as churn.
  - **First confirming observable [2026-11 / 2027-03]:** two clean quarters under the co-CEOs with no inventory glut, no step-up in discounting, and guidance met or raised.
  - **Falsifier:** founders prove operationally rusty after years as Chairmen: an inventory build, a discounting pivot, a missed guide, or a further abrupt executive exit (ties to → CLOSE trigger on governance breakdown).

- **Reported earnings understate the economics twice over: intangible investment is expensed and an FX loss masks record operating profit, so P/E screens misread the asset being compounded.**
  - **Consensus:** ~30x P/E on falling net income (−15.9% in FY2025) is an expensive, decelerating name.
  - **Variant:** the earnings decline was a CHF 173M non-cash FX loss; operating profitability set records (62.8% gross margin, 18.8% EBITDA margin). On top of that, the brand, the OAC athlete stable, Federer/Zendaya/LOEWE equity, the DTC build-out, and the LightSpray robot fleet all run through the P&L as expense, so reported invested capital and earnings understate the compounding intangible base ([G-11]). The screen that flags On as "expensive on falling earnings" is measuring FX and expensed growth investment, not economics.
  - **First confirming observable [ongoing]:** constant-currency operating metrics (cc revenue, gross margin, EBITDA margin) keep expanding while reported CHF net income stays FX-noisy: the divergence is the tell.
  - **Falsifier:** strip FX and operating margins also stall → the optics argument collapses and the deceleration is economic, not translational.

## Outstanding Questions

- **Where is the cohort data?** The entire durability case rests on repeat-purchase behavior in sticky franchises plus apparel lifting basket size, yet On discloses no cohort retention curves, LTV, CAC, or payback. Aggregate 26% growth blends new-customer acquisition (rising athlete/collaboration/retail spend) with existing-customer retention, and the two have opposite value implications ([G-12]). Answered only by On disclosing DTC cohort economics or by a third-party panel (e.g., card-spend) showing repeat rates; until then durability is an assumption, not a finding.
- **Is 23% a floor or a ceiling?** Management frames the guide as conservative and has beaten it; bears read it as the leading edge of a fade. Resolved by the trajectory of constant-currency growth across the next 3-4 quarters and by whether the US (Americas is 59% of revenue and the maturest market) holds double-digit cc growth or rolls to high-single-digits.
- **Can premium discipline survive a genuinely promotional market?** On has never faced a full demand air-pocket with Nike, Adidas, and Hoka all fighting for the same runner. Jefferies' bear framing ("premium positioning alone may not be enough to sustain price-led growth without risking demand and/or higher promotional activity") is the crux. Answered by gross-margin trajectory and any observable rise in markdowns or non-compliant discounting.
- **Does LightSpray become a cost/tariff lever or stay a halo?** The 30x capacity build is a large bet; the payoff is a mass model at a disclosed unit-cost or nearshoring benefit. Answered by which SKUs move to LightSpray and whether management quantifies the P&L impact.
- **How exposed is the "status symbol" positioning to a taste-cycle roll?** On is now described as the running world's status symbol / office-to-track aesthetic. That is precisely the fashion-adjacent positioning that cooled Under Armour, Skechers, and Nike in prior cycles. Answered only in hindsight by whether franchise reorders and new-model sell-through hold as the brand saturates.
- **What is normalized earnings power ex-FX?** With a weak USD suppressing CHF-reported results and tariffs a live drag, the market lacks a clean read on through-cycle EPS. Answered by a stabilized FX environment or by On providing clearer cc-EPS bridges.

## Business Model & Product Description

On is a Swiss premium athletic brand that outsources manufacturing and centralizes engineering, design, and brand in Zurich, closer to a design-and-IP house (think a hardware-light Apple of running) than a vertically integrated manufacturer. The economic engine is full-price discipline: minimal discounting since inception, curated wholesale doors (it closes doors that dilute presentation or pricing), and a DTC shift that together produce a ~60-64% gross margin versus Nike's 43-46% and Adidas's 48-52%, a 15-20pt gross-margin premium that is the quantitative fingerprint of the model.

**Product technology.** The core IP is CloudTec, circular rubber "cloud" pods that compress on landing then lock into a firm platform for toe-off, extended by the Speedboard plate, the Helion / Helion HF supercritical superfoam, the new CloudTec Sphere geometry (Cloudboom Strike 2, launching 2026-07-30), and LightSpray, a robot-sprayed one-piece upper. LightSpray is the strategic wildcard: capacity scaled 30-fold in 2026 (Busan factory, +32 robots), positioned as automated, low-waste, and localizable manufacturing.

**Revenue architecture.** Product is organized as durable "franchises" (nine footwear franchises each >5% of revenue) updated iteratively rather than replaced, stretching product life beyond the industry's seasonal churn and compounding brand equity per model (Cloudsurfer, Cloudmonster, Cloudrunner).

| Segmentation axis | Mix (latest) | Trajectory / economics |
|---|---|---|
| Footwear vs. apparel+accessories | ~93% / ~7% | Apparel +57.5% YoY (Q1 2026); target >10%; skews DTC (~20% of DTC vs ~7% total): a margin + acquisition lever |
| Channel: DTC vs. wholesale | 42% / 58% (from 25% / 75% in 2019) | DTC carries full assortment, higher margin; wholesale in only ~40% of Foot Locker/JD/DICK'S doors: "multiyear" white space |
| Region: Americas / EMEA / APAC | 59% / 25% / ~16-20% | APAC +61% cc (Q1 2026), China triple-digit; Americas is the maturity watch-item |
| Verticals | Running (core, fastest) + outdoor, tennis, training, all-day | Each extended into apparel; tennis originated by Federer, amplified by Shelton/Swiatek/Fonseca |

**Control structure.** IPO'd September 2021 (~$7B); founders hold ~26% economic and >50% voting via 10-vote Class B shares, insulating long-run brand-building from quarterly optics. Debt-free with >CHF 1.0B cash at year-end 2025.

## Industry Context

On sits in the design/brand layer of a ~$19-20B global running-shoe market growing ~4.8% CAGR, with performance running +8.9% YoY while lifestyle footwear declines −0.9%, a mix shift toward exactly On's technical positioning. It occupies the premium end alongside Hoka; the two are the only brands that held share through the 2022-24 industry bullwhip. The reason matters, and the source contradicts the flattering read: On avoided the glut because Vietnam/China lockdowns through H1 2022 mechanically capped its own over-ordering: the supply constraint, not the discipline, is why it had no excess inventory to clear ([[Research/2026-07-14 - ONON - On Holding Business Breakdown - deep-dive]]). "Refused to discount" and "never had to discount" are indistinguishable on the tape and worth multiples apart. Hoka's parallel resilience is the same setup (premium, lightly discounted, entering the period with momentum), so it corroborates the pattern without isolating the cause. On's one apparent stress test was a supply-constrained non-test, which is why §Outstanding Questions still records premium discipline as unproven in a genuinely promotional market.

**Competitive dynamics are intensifying precisely as On scales:**

| Competitor | 2026 posture | Read for On |
|---|---|---|
| Nike | Global sports-footwear share 22.9% (−3pts in 2025, 3rd straight decline), but running business +$1B over 5 quarters and +5 share points in running (W. Europe + N. America) in FY2026; turnaround pushed to 2027 | The most important threat: Nike is recovering specifically in running, On's core, even as it loses overall |
| Hoka (Deckers) | Decelerating to low-teens FY2026 (from 24%); Deckers stock −20% | Closest structural comp; its stall is both a warning (premium running is cyclical) and a share opportunity |
| Adidas | Record Q3 2025 (terrace/Samba-Gazelle trend) | Momentum in lifestyle; less direct in performance running |
| New Balance | Resurgent "quiet luxury" / Gen-Z; premium craftsmanship | Competes for the same premium, aesthetic-led consumer On targets |
| Asics | Performance-running strength | Direct performance competitor |

**Value chain and leverage.** On owns brand, design, and IP; it rents manufacturing (primarily Vietnam) and distributes through DTC + curated wholesale. Its leverage over wholesale partners is real (it can close doors), and its pricing power shows up as realized gross margin. But the layer it occupies is contestable: switching costs for a runner are near-zero, CloudTec/LightSpray are design-and-marketing differentiation rather than a controlled standard competitors must license, and the premium is brand rent, not a structural toll. The structural forces reshaping the industry (a shift to performance/technical product, DTC premiumization, and tariff-driven reshoring pressure) cut in On's favor on the first two and are the exact problem LightSpray is meant to answer on the third.

## Key Metrics

| Metric | Value | Notes |
|--------|-------|-------|
| Market Cap | ~$12.5B | ~$37/sh, mid-Jul 2026; 52-wk range $31.41–$54.72; consensus PT ~$57-58 (range $43–85) |
| EV/Revenue | ~3.0x TTM (~2.6x FY26E) | Net cash ~CHF 1.0B (~$1.2B), debt-free → EV ~$11.3B; FY26E rev ≥CHF 3.44B |
| Revenue Growth | +30% FY2025 reported / +35.6% cc; +26.4% cc Q1 2026; guide ≥23% cc FY2026 | Reported held back by strong CHF / weak USD |
| Gross Margin | 64.2% Q1 2026 (62.8% FY2025); guide ≥64.5% FY2026 | After absorbing a 20% Vietnam→US tariff ($70M in Q1) |
| FCF Yield | ~2.9% (FCF ~$358M TTM / ~$12.5B mcap) | Adj EBITDA margin 21.0% Q1 (18.8% FY2025); fwd P/E ~21-25x; EV/EBITDA ~16x |

## Management and culture

Hypothesis: Weak fit on [[Lens - Management and Culture]]: Gate 1 passes on a high-cadence product/brand optionality feed (franchise iteration, apparel, adjacent sports, LightSpray, APAC); Gate 2 is only partial because the 2026 de-rate, the 2026-03-25 −11% founder-CEO print, and the 2026-08-11 −19% Q2 print price the pipeline as fade, yet ~21–25x still embeds a growth compounder. [MC-2] 2025 Compensation Report (filed 2026-03-03): founders moved to 100% PSUs (no salary, no cash bonus, CHF 2.9M target LTI each, ~92% variable), vesting on Net Sales CAGR and Adj. EBITDA CAGR plus relative TSR, not ROIC or product-volume; YE2025 three-founder 12.8% economic / 52.9% votes via 10-vote Class B. Clustered open-market buys: 2026-05-14 each founder 60,000 Class A (~$2.2M at ~$36.64); 2026-08-14 Coppetti and Bernhard 65,000 each at $30.67. [MC-7]/§4: 2026-05-01 Allemann and Coppetti re-took co-CEO after Maurer (2025-04-01) and Hoffmann (2026-05-01) exited; LightSpray scaler Scott Maguire promoted to President & COO over the full value chain: product/functional, not matrix. [MC-6] 3,963 FTE YE2025 (+22% vs 3,254; retail 1,230 vs 808) under the ~5k heuristic; two CEO exits in 13 months is entropy until two clean quarters prove calibration. [MC-6]/[G-10] adversary: footwear brands fade and founder-returns rust; sales-plus-EBITDA incentives maximise growth, not capital return, in a taste-cycle category. Swing variable: two clean founder-CEO quarters with no inventory glut or discounting.

## Bull Case

On sustains 23-28% constant-currency growth through 2028 on four independent runways: APAC/China (triple-digit, "very much at the beginning"), apparel (+50%+, toward >10% of revenue), US white space (in only ~40% of key wholesale doors; ~75% of its own markets still don't know the brand), and DTC premiumization, while holding a 64%+ gross margin and pushing EBITDA margin above 20%. LightSpray scales from halo to mass models, localizing production and converting the tariff drag into a cost advantage. The "fade" fear proves wrong, and the market re-rates the multiple back toward its own consensus. Framework: if FY2027 revenue reaches ~CHF 4.2-4.5B (~$5.3-5.6B) at a 20%+ EBITDA margin (~$1.1B EBITDA) and durability re-rates the stock to 20-22x EBITDA, EV moves to ~$22-24B, roughly +90% from ~$11.3B EV, consistent with the $57-58 consensus target and the $70-85 bull-case targets (BTIG $70). The de-rating means the bull case now requires only that On keep doing what it is already doing, not a re-acceleration.

## Bear Case

23% is the first visible step of a fade, and the footwear base rate reasserts. Growth decelerates to mid-teens (2026) → low-teens (2027) → high-single-digits (2028) as the ~CHF 3B base scales and the "status symbol" taste cycle rolls over, the exact path that cooled Under Armour, Skechers, and Nike's own cycles. Competitive intensity does the rest: Nike's running recovery (+5 share points already), Adidas's momentum, New Balance's premium pull, and a defending Hoka force On off full-price discipline; markdowns rise, and the 64% gross margin unwinds toward the high-50s. FX (weak USD) keeps suppressing reported CHF results and sentiment; the double management change plus a new CFO produces an execution stumble under founders who have been Chairmen, not operators, for years; the Vietnam tariff stays a live earnings drag and LightSpray stays a sub-1% halo. In that world, the multiple compresses further: a decelerating brand loses its growth multiple. If cc growth falls to low-teens and the stock re-rates to ~15x P/E on ~$1.30 EPS, the shares are ~$20 (roughly −45%), and a broken growth narrative can take it below the $31.41 low well before that. The absence of any disclosed cohort/LTV data means neither On nor the investor can prove the retention that would refute this; the burden of proof sits with the bull.

## Catalysts

- **Q2 2026 earnings (~mid-Aug 2026)**: the key near-term test: Americas/US cc growth trajectory, whether ≥23% is beaten/raised again, inventory and discounting discipline under the new co-CEOs. Both directions.
- **LightSpray Cloudboom Strike 2 launch (2026-07-30)** and subsequent LightSpray mass-model signals: read on whether the platform moves beyond halo.
- **Q3 2026 earnings (~Nov 2026)**: holiday sell-through + China trajectory.
- **FY2026 results + FY2027 guide (~March 2027)**: first full year under founder co-CEOs; tests the post-2026 "20-25% growth / 20%+ EBITDA margin" ambition.
- **Insider activity**: further founder buying (bullish confirmation) or any selling (bearish).
- **Negative/macro:** USD/CHF moves, tariff escalation or refund resolution, competitor product cycles (Nike running push, Adidas), any further abrupt executive exits.

## Risks

- **Thesis risk: taste-cycle peak (central).** On is a contestable consumer brand with near-zero switching costs and no layer moat; if the brand cools, growth and margin fade to the footwear base rate. This is the single risk that breaks the compounder thesis.
- **Thesis risk: premium discipline breaks.** If intensifying competition forces On to discount to hold volume, the 64% gross margin (the load-bearing datapoint of the whole model) compresses and the premium-brand economics unwind.
- **Thesis risk: founder-operator execution failure.** A double leadership change plus a new CFO raises the odds of strategic drift, an inventory misstep, or a discounting pivot in the next 2-4 quarters.
- **Position risk: FX.** On reports in CHF; a weak USD suppresses reported results and sentiment regardless of underlying demand, and can drive the stock independent of the thesis.
- **Position risk: tariffs.** Vietnam sourcing concentration makes the 20% US tariff a live, ongoing earnings drag; escalation would hurt before LightSpray nearshoring can offset it.
- **Position risk: multiple compression.** Even if growth holds, a growth-brand multiple can de-rate further in a risk-off rotation.

## Conviction Triggers

- **→ HIGH if**: two consecutive quarters of >25% cc growth with gross margin sustained ≥64% AND disclosed evidence of repeat-purchase / DTC cohort-retention strength (or a credible third-party panel proxy) confirming durability beats the base rate; OR a LightSpray mass-market model ships at volume with a disclosed unit-cost / tariff benefit.
- **→ LOW if**: two consecutive quarters of sub-20% cc growth absent a macro shock, OR gross margin falls below ~60% on rising promotional activity (premium discipline breaking).
- **→ CLOSE if**: cc growth falls to high-single-digits AND the company begins systematic discounting (taste-cycle-peak thesis-breaker confirmed), OR a founder-operator governance breakdown (further abrupt executive exits / a strategy reversal).

## Mental Models

- **Models applied**: [[Mental Models/Generalist - Overview]] (always) · [[Mental Models/Lens - Value Layer Monopoly]] · [[Mental Models/Lens - Automation & AI Readiness]] · [[Lens - Management and Culture]]. No matching `Industry -` note exists for athletic footwear/apparel.
- **Triggers that fired** (each a hypothesis to test, not a verdict):
  - Generalist [G-13] · expectations-investing: the price embeds a fade (23% guide vs. a history of beats); the mispriced variable is growth-durability, and the ~3x EV/revenue de-rate may have over-corrected.
  - Generalist [G-10] · base rates / outside view: sustaining >20% CAGR off a ~CHF 3B base is a rare justified-outlier bet; the footwear reference class fades hard. The adversarial anchor against the compounder narrative.
  - Generalist [G-6] · pricing power: 64% gross margin on minimal discounting is realized pricing power; test whether it is structural or brand-cycle rent.
  - Generalist [G-11] · intangibles expensed: brand/athlete/retail/LightSpray spend is expensed and an FX loss masks record operating profit; reported P/E misreads the compounding asset.
  - Generalist [G-12] · cohort economics: the decisive durability data (retention curve, LTV/CAC) is undisclosed; the central gap a durability thesis must source.
  - Generalist [G-5]/[G-8] · corporate quality & capital allocation: founder control (>50% votes, ~26% economic), founders re-taking operations and buying at the lows; a governance positive the market prices as churn-risk.
  - Generalist [G-3] · mean-reversion vs. trend: the meta-question: compounder (trend) or late-cycle taste brand (mean-revert)? Unresolved, and the most expensive error to get wrong either way.
  - Value Layer Monopoly · **NO / WEAK FIT (hypothesis)**: application-layer consumer brand; low switching costs; CloudTec/LightSpray are design/marketing differentiation, not a standard/interface others must traverse and pay to cross; premium is rentable, not a layer toll. AI-era overlay: application-layer (moat-dissolving direction), though consumer-brand moats are less AI-exposed than software. A disconfirming lens against any "moat" language.
  - Automation & AI Readiness · **WEAK Lens A (operator) fit (hypothesis)**: LightSpray robotic manufacturing is a genuine labor/waste-reduction and nearshoring/tariff-hedge lever, but the consumer/physical-goods sector overlay is "hardest, most bounded," so cap the automation-margin upside and hold this as a watch-item, not a confirmed thesis leg.
  - Management & Culture [MC-1] · gates: Gate 1 pass (product/brand optionality feed); Gate 2 partial (de-rate + founder-CEO selloff + Q2 dump price the pipeline as fade, not a capture premium).
  - Management & Culture [MC-2] · incentive duration / ownership: 100% PSU founders (2025), dual-class 12.8% economic / 52.9% votes, clustered open-market buys May and Aug 2026; metrics are sales+EBITDA+TSR, not ROIC.
  - Management & Culture [MC-6] · bureaucratic entropy: 3,963 FTE YE2025 (+22% YoY; retail 1,230 vs 808); two CEO exits in 13 months is the default forecast until calibration is evidenced.
  - Management & Culture [MC-7] · org polarity / founder return: Maguire COO over the full value chain is product/functional scale-up; 2026-05-01 founder co-CEO return is a §4 transition, not yet a calibrated turnaround.
- **Disconfirming check**: every bull lens (pricing power, founder quality, share gains, cheap-vs-its-own-history) points the same way, which by the READING PROTOCOL is the cue to hunt the bear hardest. The single falsifying datapoint: the first two-quarter run of sub-20% cc growth without a macro shock, or gross margin cracking below 60%: either confirms the [G-10] footwear base rate and the [Value Layer Monopoly] "melting brand asset" read over the compounder narrative. The base rate this thesis must beat: few firms hold >20% revenue CAGR for a decade, and the rate collapses as the base grows. The [G-12] cohort/LTV data is the only thing that could resolve it in the bull's favor before the tape does; until it is disclosed, durability is an assumption. The Weak-fit [MC] claim must also beat [MC-6] organisational entropy (two CEO exits, 22% headcount growth, sales-plus-EBITDA incentives) and the [G-10] founder-return / footwear-brand fade base rate: a Strong-fit upgrade is not earned until two clean founder-CEO quarters falsify rust.

# [134/159] Theses/ONTO - Onto Innovation.md
**thesis · ticker: ONTO · status: draft · conviction: medium · sector: Advanced Semi Metrology · date: 2026-06-22 · metrics as of: 2026-07-12 · tags: thesis, semiconductor-capital-equipment, advanced-semi-metrology, advanced-packaging, ONTO · source: Onto Innovation Q1 2026 results (8-K + earnings call, May 5 2026) + FY2025/FY2024 results + vault synthesis ([[Macro & Technology/CoWoS-to-CoPoS Panel-Level Packaging Transition]], [[Sectors/Advanced Semi Metrology]], [[Theses/KLA - KLA Corporation]]); web research 2026-06-22**

## Summary

The vault flagged ONTO as the cheapest, highest-leverage uncovered name in the CoWoS→CoPoS panel-packaging transition: the only process-control vendor that also patterns the panel. The market got there first: ONTO is +174% over twelve months to ~$336 (~$16.6B cap), re-rated from the ~24x "value or value-trap" laggard of the metrology trio (per the vault's own late-May sector note) to ~46x forward / ~65x trailing, with the sell-side at "Strong Buy" but an average target only ~5% above spot. The investable question is therefore no longer "is ONTO cheap" (that entry is gone) but "does a genuine CoPoS call-option plus 50%+ advanced-packaging growth justify a compounder multiple on the sub-scale, most-contestable member of a field that KLA is actively invading?" The non-consensus answer: the panel-lithography franchise (JetStep, qualified at two AI-packaging suppliers, ramping 2027) is a real asymmetric option round-wafer steppers physically cannot replicate, and ONTO's path-agnostic breadth (inspection + metrology + litho + software, earning on CoWoS, CoPoS and CoWoP) is undervalued by the "spread-thin sub-scale" framing, but that same breadth caps its margin and scale in every niche, KLA takes the high-resolution HBM4/hybrid-bond tier where the profit concentrates, and US manufacturing structurally cedes the fastest-localizing China AP market to Camtek. Medium conviction: own the structural exposure the vault wants, but at 46x the margin of safety is in the optionality, not the price.

## Key Non-consensus Insights

**1. The vault's own "cheap value play" thesis is already dead, and that repricing is the most important fact about ONTO today.** The [[Sectors/Advanced Semi Metrology]] sector note (2026-05-27) frames ONTO as "the cheapest of the four (~24x P/E): either a value opportunity or a correct read on structural scale disadvantage." Four weeks later the market has resolved that question by re-rating ONTO up: ~46x forward (on ~$7.22 2026E non-GAAP EPS), ~65x trailing, +174% in a year, with the Street's average price target now only ~5% above spot. The "value" leg of the case has been arbitraged away in real time on the CoPoS/panel-packaging narrative. This matters because every downstream judgment inverts: a sub-scale challenger trading at a discount is a margin-of-safety setup where the option is free; the same challenger trading at a premium-compounder multiple is a setup where you are paying KLA-adjacent multiples for a business with none of KLA's monopoly economics, defect-library moat, or ~$4B service annuity. The thesis is no longer "buy the cheap one"; it is "is the panel-litho optionality worth a full multiple re-rate," and the honest answer is partially.

**2. JetStep panel lithography is an asymmetric call-option the metrology-trio framing structurally cannot see.** The standard frame (Onto vs Nova vs Camtek vs KLA) is an inspection-and-metrology comparison, and on that axis ONTO is sub-scale. But ONTO is the only one of the four with a panel-lithography franchise, and panel litho is the one CoPoS layer where incumbent round-wafer steppers (ASML/Canon/Nikon wafer tools) physically do not apply: die-shift, CTE mismatch and panel warpage on a 600×600mm+ rectangular panel require a purpose-built tool. JetStep (S3500 / X500, exposing CCL, FR4, composite and glass up to 720×600mm) is exactly that tool, and management disclosed it is **already qualified at two packaging suppliers to AI device manufacturers with a 2027 ramp**. The asymmetry: ONTO sizes the whole panel-level franchise (JetStep + Firefly) at only ~$200M against a >$1.3B 2026 base, small enough that the market discounts it, but with "meaningful upside if industry adoption accelerates." If TSMC's CoPoS pilot (VisEra ~June 2026, AP7 HVM 2028-29) ramps as the companion macro note now argues, panel litho is a multi-hundred-million franchise where ONTO has a first-mover qualification lead and incumbents are still adapting wafer tools. You are not paying much for this option inside 46x; that is the part of the re-rate that is justified.

**3. ONTO's advanced-packaging growth is real but structurally margin-capped ("high-volume, margin-capped growth," not monopoly economics), because the AP collision resolves on resolution, not price.** AP is genuinely inflecting: >50% growth guided for 2026, 3Di winning 10+ orders in Q1 on sub-6μm bump adoption (vs 15-25μm historically), Dragonfly G5 (150nm defect sensitivity) with a 15+ application pipeline across 10+ customers, a >$240M HBM volume-purchase agreement through 2027. But the binding structural fact (per [[Sectors/Advanced Semi Metrology]] and [[Theses/KLA - KLA Corporation]]) is that a missed defect at HBM4 16-Hi / hybrid-bonding scraps a multi-thousand-dollar stacked package, so the highest-resolution inspector wins the highest-value work regardless of price, and at the sub-0.5nm copper-recess tier that is KLA, whose AP revenue grew 70% to $950M precisely by invading this zone. ONTO's durable territory is the cost-sensitive mid-range plus the litho/films-metrology adjacencies KLA doesn't contest (Iris films metrology, 3Di, JetStep). That territory grows in volume with every HBM die-stack, but not in pricing power. The market is extrapolating AP unit growth into a compounder multiple; the correct read is high-growth, structurally-lower-incremental-margin work beneath a competitor who takes the cream.

**4. The "Onto + Camtek = ~65% of AP inspection" headline hides a geographic asymmetry that caps ONTO's real AP TAM.** The duopoly framing treats ONTO and Camtek as interchangeable co-leaders. They are not: ONTO manufactures in the US and faces tightening export-control friction selling advanced-packaging tools into mainland China, while Camtek (Israel) ships into China (the single fastest-localizing, highest-volume AP market) with far less constraint. China is where mature-node and OSAT AP capacity is being built out most aggressively and where domestic substitution is policy-driven. The consequence: a structurally meaningful slice of the AP-inspection TAM is effectively Camtek's and the domestic entrants' to win, not ONTO's, and ONTO's addressable AP market is smaller than the global share figure implies. The sell-side models "AP duopoly, both win"; the geography says ONTO's AP runway is narrower and more US/Korea/Taiwan-concentrated than Camtek's, a quiet structural disadvantage that widens if export controls tighten further.

**5. The diversification the trio-framing penalizes as "spread-thin R&D" is simultaneously ONTO's best hedge and the reason it stays sub-scale; bull and bear are the same fact.** ONTO spans inspection (Dragonfly) + metrology (Atlas, Iris) + lithography (JetStep) + analytics (Discover), front-end GAA and back-end packaging. The pure-play critique is that this spreads a ~$1.3B revenue base and a sub-KLA R&D budget across four fronts, leaving it second-best in each. That same breadth makes ONTO genuinely path-agnostic: it earns whether the winning format is CoWoS, CoPoS, or CoWoP, whether the substrate is organic or glass, and whether intensity grows fastest in GAA logic metrology (Atlas G6, 2nd logic GAA customer won, ~25% advanced-nodes growth) or HBM/AP. In a transition whose format and material winner is still unresolved (per the companion CoPoS macro note), optionality across all paths is worth more than depth in one, but it is also precisely why ONTO will never have KLA's defect-library moat or Camtek's China-AP volume. The investor who resolves this correctly sizes ONTO as a transition-optionality position, not a quality-compounder.

## Outstanding Questions

**1. Did ONTO actually fail TSMC's CoWoS-L qualification at the tighter bump pitch, as the most credible bear alleges?** The sharpest short take (irrationalanalysis "Onto Innovation Implosion") claims ONTO "failed TSMC qualification for CoWoS-L" and that KLA's repurposed process-control tools "crush Onto" in AP inspection. If true at the leading-edge 2.5D node, ONTO's AP growth is concentrated in the trailing tier and far more contestable than the >50% headline suggests. If false, and Q1 disclosed Dragonfly G5 qualification "at a leading 2.5D logic customer", the bear is overstated. *Resolution: TSMC CoWoS/CoPoS tool-of-record disclosures, ONTO's named-customer AP qual scorecard through 2026, SEMICON West (July 2026) competitive intelligence.*

**2. What is the panel-lithography TAM at CoPoS HVM, and what share does ONTO actually hold once ASML/Canon/Nikon/SCREEN field panel tools?** ONTO's ~$200M panel-level expectation is a 2026-2027 qual/pilot number. If CoPoS reaches AP7 HVM in 2028-29, the panel-litho TAM could be multiples larger, but ASML, Canon, Nikon and SCREEN are all developing PLP-capable systems, and ONTO's first-mover lead is not a monopoly. *Resolution: TSMC CoPoS panel-litho tool selections at AP7/VisEra, ONTO panel-level backlog trajectory, competitor panel-tool announcements.*

**3. Is the Q1 GAAP gross-margin compression (50.1% vs 53.7% a year ago) a mix/amortization artifact or an early pricing-power signal?** Non-GAAP GM held/expanded (55.7%) and Q2 is guided to 56-56.5%, but the GAAP delta plus management's flag of "increasing headwinds around certain material costs, fuel charges" warrants watching as KLA and Camtek compete in overlapping AP categories. *Resolution: GAAP-to-non-GAAP bridge in the 10-Q, GM trajectory through 2026, any ASP commentary.*

**4. How much of 2026's >30% growth is a structural intensity step versus a cyclical AP-capex peak?** ONTO printed a near-flat 2025 ($1.005B, +1.8%) before a +30% 2026 guide, a sharp inflection that maps to the AI-packaging capex wave. At 46x forward, the multiple assumes the step is structural and durable. If 2026 is an AP-capex peak that digests in 2027 (as HBM/CoWoS allocation normalizes), both estimates and multiple compress together. *Resolution: 2027 order trajectory, TSMC/SK Hynix AP capex guidance, backlog composition.*

**5. Can Discover software ever become a KLA-Klarity-style annuity, or is software/services permanently a sub-scale ~20% line?** KLA's re-rate to compounder status rests on a ~$4B recurring service+software annuity with data lock-in. ONTO's software & services is ~18.5-23% of revenue and lacks the cross-customer defect corpus. Whether Discover can build genuine switching-cost stickiness is the swing factor between "ONTO is a hardware-cyclical at 46x" and "ONTO is an emerging compounder." *Resolution: software attach-rate and recurring-mix disclosures, Discover installed-base growth.*

**6. Is the >$240M HBM volume-purchase agreement through 2027 incremental demand or a pull-forward?** A multi-year VPA is a backlog-visibility positive, but if it front-loads HBM metrology demand it flatters 2026-27 at the expense of a 2028 air-pocket. *Resolution: backlog disclosures, whether further VPAs are signed, HBM4→HBM5 transition timing.*

**7. How fast does China export-control tightening erode ONTO's accessible AP market versus Camtek's?** If US controls extend to more AP/mature-node tooling, ONTO loses TAM that Camtek and domestic entrants capture. *Resolution: BIS rule changes, ONTO China revenue mix trajectory, Camtek China share.*

## Business Model & Product Description

Onto Innovation sells the inspection, metrology, lithography and yield-analytics tools that semiconductor manufacturers use to find defects, measure features, pattern panels and manage yield, concentrated in the two fastest-growing pockets of process control: **advanced packaging** (2.5D/3D, HBM, CoWoS/CoPoS) and **advanced nodes** (gate-all-around logic, advanced DRAM). ONTO is a yield auditor like KLA, but the only one that also owns a printing press for the panel. Where KLA is the full-spectrum front-end inspection monopoly and Nova/Camtek are pure metrology / AP-inspection specialists, ONTO is the diversified mid-scale generalist: broadest portfolio, sub-scale in each lane, and uniquely holding a lithography franchise that gives it a foothold in AP patterning, not just measurement. Formed from the 2019 merger of Rudolph Technologies (inspection + AP litho) and Nanometrics (OCD/film metrology), the breadth is structural DNA.

**Revenue segmentation** (FY2025 ~$1.005B; the economics are best captured by ONTO's three reported lines):

| Segment | FY2025 | % of rev | 2026E growth | What it is |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Specialty Devices & Advanced Packaging | ~$500M+ | ~50% | AP sub-line **>50%**; specialty soft (~$25M/qtr) | Dragonfly inspection, Iris films metrology, 3Di 3D metrology, JetStep panel litho: the AI/HBM/CoWoS engine; specialty (power/RF/CIS/mature) is the cyclical drag, now a minor tail |
| Advanced Nodes | ~$300M (2× the $148.5M of FY2024) | ~30% | **~25%** | Atlas G6 OCD/film metrology for GAA logic + HBM4 / advanced DRAM; 2nd logic GAA customer won; new TSV-metrology application |
| Software & Services | ~$185-230M | ~18-23% | steady | Discover analytics + installed-base service; the (small) annuity gesture toward KLA's model |

**Key products:**
- **Dragonfly G5**: macro/AP inspection, 150nm defect sensitivity, extensible to next-gen nodes; shipments began Q1 2026 ahead of schedule; qualified at a leading 2.5D logic customer and a leading HBM maker for HBM4; 15+ application pipeline across 10+ customers. The AP inspection workhorse.
- **Atlas G6**: OCD/thin-film metrology for gate-all-around logic and HBM4 DRAM; selected by a second logic GAA customer; new TSV-metrology win (2H 2026 shipments). The advanced-nodes growth driver.
- **Iris**: films metrology; a stated driver of the AP growth alongside Dragonfly.
- **3Di**: 3D metrology for advanced packaging; 10+ incremental orders in Q1 on sub-6μm microbump adoption (the smaller the bump, the higher the metrology intensity).
- **JetStep S3500 / X500**: panel-level packaging lithography; 59.4×59.4mm exposure field, 2/2 L/S resolution (option to 1/1), substrates to 720×600mm including CCL/FR4/composite/**glass**; corrects die-shift, CTE mismatch, panel warpage. The CoPoS optionality; qualified at two AI-packaging suppliers, 2027 ramp. JetStep + Firefly panel franchise sized ~$200M with upside on CoPoS adoption.
- **Discover**: analytics/yield software; ONTO's sub-scale answer to KLA's Klarity/RAPID.

**Customers** (mid-2024 concentration): TSMC ~23%, Samsung ~20%, SK Hynix ~13% (~56% top-three): a leading-edge logic + HBM/DRAM customer base, plus mature/mid-node logic, memory, power and OSATs (a slice of which is China-constrained for AP tools).

**Balance sheet:** net cash ~$850M ($852M cash + short-term investments end-FY2024, $0 long-term debt), FY2024 FCF $213.8M, ~150% cash conversion of non-GAAP net income in Q4 2025: financially unlevered and self-funding, which de-risks the R&D-across-four-fronts model.

## Industry Context

ONTO sits in **process control**: the inspection + metrology sub-stratum of wafer-fab equipment, structurally the fastest-growing slice of WFE (PC% rising from ~9% at 28nm toward 16-19% at 2nm/1.4nm) because every architectural transition (FinFET→GAA→CFET, monolithic→HBM stacking→hybrid bonding) adds inspection/measurement passes without removing any. The defining structural fact of the sub-sector (per [[Sectors/Advanced Semi Metrology]]): **process control is not one market**; it is a leading-edge inspection monopoly (KLA, 56-63% PC share, defect-library + Klarity/RAPID software moat) bolted to a contestable metrology field (Nova, ONTO) and an emerging advanced-packaging battleground (ONTO, Camtek) that KLA is now invading. ONTO holds ~6-8% of total process control but co-leads AP inspection with Camtek (~65% combined).

**Where ONTO sits in the value chain and who has leverage:**
- Customers (TSMC, Samsung, SK Hynix, Intel, Micron, OSATs) have **low** pricing power at the leading edge (12-24 month tool-of-record qualification, switching costs in the millions per tool per node) but **moderate** power in AP and at mature nodes where ONTO, Camtek and Chinese alternatives provide partial substitutes, i.e., exactly ONTO's mix is the part of process control where customers can push back hardest.
- The AP collision is the defining competitive dynamic: KLA's defect-resolution edge at HBM4 16-Hi / hybrid-bonding (sub-0.5nm copper-recess) means a KLA-takes-the-high-end, specialists-hold-the-cost-sensitive-mid-range split rather than winner-take-all. ONTO grows in absolute terms (every HBM stack multiplies touchpoints) but the highest-margin work concentrates with KLA.
- The panel-litho new layer is where ONTO has genuine structural advantage: round-wafer steppers cannot pattern rectangular panels, so JetStep competes against adapted Canon/Nikon/SCREEN/ASML panel efforts from a first-mover qualification position rather than against an entrenched monopoly. This is the one layer where ONTO is offense, not defense.
- The integration / bundling threat (AMAT PVI in-line metrology, LRCX Equipment Intelligence, ASML eScan) pressures standalone metrology (ONTO's Atlas/Iris lines) more than inspection or litho, a slow-moving TAM compressor at mature/mid nodes.

**Structural forces reshaping the sub-sector:** AP TAM-creation (bond-line, copper-recess, panel categories that did not exist before ~2022); GAA→CFET metrology-intensity step; HBM4→HBM5 hybrid-bonding (sub-10μm bump pitch → ~3x bond-line inspection intensity per [[Research/2026-05-11 - HBM Packaging Equipment Stack - MR-MUF to Hybrid Bonding Transition - deep-dive]]); the CoWoS→CoPoS format transition (now accelerated to 2028-29 HVM per the companion macro note); and the China substitution asymmetry that favors Camtek over ONTO in AP.

**Panel-level packaging: ONTO's actual CoPoS position.** Direct answers to the three questions the panel-litho leg of this thesis turns on:

*Share: there is none to measure yet.* CoPoS is pre-HVM: TSMC's pilot line completes ~June 2026 (VisEra), pilot production 2027, mass production 2H 2028-29 (AP7 Chiayi). There is no share to hold of a market that does not yet ship in volume. ONTO's real position is a **first-mover qualification lead in panel lithography, the one panel layer where round-wafer steppers physically do not apply**: JetStep qualified at two packaging suppliers to AI device makers, 2027 ramp. On the panel market that exists today (FOPLP for PMIC/RF at up to 620×750mm), ONTO's entire panel franchise (JetStep + Firefly) is ~$200M, <15% of 2026E revenue. ONTO is the presumptive front-runner in the uncontested-by-physics layer, not the holder of a measurable CoPoS production share.

*Uniqueness: yes for patterning, no for measurement; the question splits by process step.*

| Panel step | ONTO tool | Uniquely qualified? |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Lithography (patterning) | JetStep S3500/X500 | **Yes by physics, not by monopoly.** Round-wafer steppers (ASML/Canon/Nikon) cannot expose a 600mm+ rectangular panel or correct die-shift / CTE-mismatch / warpage. JetStep is purpose-built for it, but the lead is first-mover qualification, contestable by SUSS MicroTec and adapted Canon/Nikon/SCREEN panel tools, not a structural lock-in. |
| Inspection / metrology | Dragonfly, Iris, 3Di | **No: normal competition.** Adapt to panel format (the "double exposure" alongside litho) but compete head-on with KLA (high-resolution tier) and Camtek (mid-range / China). |

*Growth: a sized call-option, not a base case.* Scenarios against the ~$200M base:

| Scenario | Franchise by ~2028-29 | Condition |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Stagnation | ~$200M | CoPoS slips past 2029, or Canon/Nikon/SUSS capture the panel-litho share ONTO pioneered |
| Base | ~$350-450M | Two qualified suppliers convert to 2027 volume; ONTO holds a plurality as CoPoS reaches 515mm HVM (~20 interposers/panel, 12-16 HBM stacks) |
| Bull | ~$600M+ | JetStep becomes panel-litho tool-of-record at AP7; TAM compounds along the 310→515→750mm panel roadmap; Firefly/inspection attach rides along |

Even the bull case (~3x today) is ~30-40% of current revenue: differentiated, not company-transforming on its own. The larger engine stays AP inspection/metrology (>50% 2026E) and advanced nodes (~25%); panel litho is the asymmetric option layered on top, which is why the HIGH conviction trigger keys on panel backlog crossing ~$350M. Its value is not its size today but that it is the one layer where ONTO plays offense against incumbents who must re-tool, not defense against a monopoly that out-resolves it.

## Bull Case

ONTO compounds through 2028 as the diversified picks-and-shovels winner of two intensity waves plus a format-transition option:

(a) **AP sustains >50% growth and broadens**: Dragonfly G5 ramps across its 15+ application / 10+ customer pipeline, 3Di rides sub-6μm bump adoption, Iris films metrology scales, and the >$240M HBM VPA anchors 2026-27 visibility. AP becomes a durable >$750M franchise.

(b) **Advanced nodes compounds ~25%**: Atlas G6 wins broaden across GAA logic (2nd customer secured) and HBM4/advanced DRAM, with TSV metrology a new leg; advanced nodes doubles again toward $400-450M as 2nm GAA HVM and HBM4 DRAM ramp.

(c) **The panel-litho option pays off**: TSMC's CoPoS pilot (VisEra ~June 2026) confirms panel-format litho demand; JetStep converts its two qualified AI-packaging suppliers into volume in 2027 and wins CoPoS panel-litho tool-of-record positions into the AP7 2028-29 HVM ramp. The ~$200M panel franchise re-rates to a multi-hundred-million growth driver in a layer where round-wafer incumbents cannot directly compete.

(d) **Margins inflect**: operating margin crosses 30% by Q4 2026 and holds, non-GAAP GM stays 56%+, and the net-cash balance sheet funds R&D-across-four-fronts without dilution.

**Valuation framework:** if 2026 lands >$1.3B (+30%) and 2027 grows ~20% to ~$1.6B at >30% OM, non-GAAP EPS reaches ~$9-10 in 2027. Holding ~40x (a slight de-rate from 46x as growth normalizes) → ~$360-400; sustaining 46x on accelerating panel-litho optionality → ~$420-460 (+25-37%). The bull case is a quality-of-growth re-rate: the market reclassifies ONTO from "sub-scale challenger" to "path-agnostic transition winner with a unique litho call-option," and the multiple holds while earnings compound.

## Bear Case

ONTO de-rates hard as the AP-capex wave digests and the competitive reality reasserts:

(a) **KLA crushes the high end and the duopoly story cracks**: the sharpest short take alleges ONTO failed TSMC CoWoS-L qualification at the tighter bump pitch and that KLA's repurposed process-control tools out-resolve ONTO wherever they are pointed at AP inspection. KLA's AP revenue (+70% to $950M) is taking exactly the highest-value HBM4/hybrid-bond work; ONTO is left with cost-sensitive, margin-capped mid-range volume. The "Onto + Camtek = 65%" share erodes as KLA invades from the top and China-domestic entrants take the bottom.

(b) **China is structurally Camtek's, not ONTO's**: US manufacturing blocks ONTO from selling AP tools freely into mainland China, the fastest-localizing, highest-volume AP market; Camtek ships there at scale. A slice of ONTO's modeled AP TAM is unwinnable, and tightening export controls widen the gap.

(c) **2026 is an AP-capex peak, not a structural step**: after a flat 2025 (+1.8%), the +30% 2026 guide is a cyclical AI-packaging spike. 2027 digests; AP growth decelerates below +20%; advanced-nodes orders normalize after the GAA pull-forward; the HBM VPA proves to have front-loaded demand.

(d) **The multiple is the position's own worst enemy**: at ~46x forward / ~65x trailing after a +174% run, with the Street's target only ~5% above spot and the P/E ~326% above its 5-year median, ONTO prices in flawless execution. Any guide-down, GAAP-margin slip (already 50.1% vs 53.7%), or panel-litho timing slip triggers multiple compression and estimate cuts simultaneously, the classic high-multiple semicap drawdown. Past cyclical lows show the downside volatility is severe; a re-rate to even 28-30x forward on flat 2027 estimates is ~-35% to -40%.

(e) **Panel-litho optionality fails to convert**: CoPoS slips right (TSMC panel-yield miss pushes HVM past 2029), or ASML/Canon/Nikon take the panel-litho share ONTO pioneered, and the ~$200M franchise stays ~$200M. The single most differentiated piece of the bull case evaporates.

The world where ONTO loses money: you buy the vault's "uncovered panel-litho gap" after the market already paid up for it, the AP cycle rolls over in 2027, KLA confirms high-end AP dominance, and the 46x multiple halves.

## Risks

**Thesis risks** (the investment case is wrong):

1. **KLA captures the high-resolution AP tier and reduces ONTO to margin-capped mid-range volume.** KLA's defect-library + sub-0.5nm resolution win the HBM4/hybrid-bond work where profit concentrates; ONTO's AP growth comes at structurally lower incremental margins than 46x implies. If the bear's "failed CoWoS-L qualification" allegation is accurate at the leading edge, this is already underway. *Resolution: named AP tool-of-record disclosures, GM trajectory, SEMICON West intelligence.*

2. **The AP-capex wave is cyclical and 2026 is the peak.** A flat-2025 / +30%-2026 / digesting-2027 shape would crater both estimates and the multiple. ONTO's near-pure exposure to AI-packaging and HBM capex makes it a high-beta cyclical dressed as a structural compounder. *Resolution: 2027 orders, TSMC/SK Hynix AP capex guidance, backlog mix.*

3. **Panel-litho optionality fails to convert**: CoPoS slips past 2029 or incumbents (ASML/Canon/Nikon/SCREEN) take panel-litho share; the ~$200M franchise stagnates and the most differentiated part of the bull case is worthless. *Resolution: CoPoS pilot milestones, JetStep backlog, competitor panel-tool wins.*

4. **China AP TAM erosion**: export-control tightening cedes more of the fastest-growing AP market to Camtek and domestic entrants. *Resolution: BIS rules, ONTO China mix, Camtek share.*

**Position risks** (thesis is right but the stock falls anyway):

5. **Multiple compression from the ~46x forward / ~65x trailing starting point.** With the Street target only ~5% above spot and the P/E ~326% above its 5-year median, a sector de-rate, AI-capex-deflation narrative, or rotation out of high-multiple semis is a -30%+ drawdown on no fundamental change. The valuation is the position risk.

6. **Customer concentration**: TSMC + Samsung + SK Hynix ~56% of revenue; any single-customer capex pause or a Taiwan/Korea tail event removes a large revenue slice abruptly.

7. **GAAP-margin and cost headwinds**: Q1 GAAP GM already fell to 50.1% (from 53.7%) on material/fuel/shipping costs; sustained input pressure dents the margin-inflection narrative the multiple depends on.

## Conviction Triggers

→ **HIGH if** any two: TSMC names ONTO JetStep as a CoPoS panel-litho tool-of-record at AP7/VisEra (or discloses ONTO panel tools in the pilot line) **+** ONTO panel-level (JetStep + Firefly) backlog/guidance exceeds ~$350M (vs ~$200M base) **+** AP segment sustains >50% YoY for two consecutive quarters with non-GAAP GM held ≥56% **+** a named win displacing KLA at a leading 2.5D/HBM customer.

→ **LOW if** any one: KLA wins a disclosed AP inspection/metrology tool-of-record displacing ONTO at TSMC / SK Hynix / a leading 2.5D customer **OR** combined AP + advanced-nodes YoY growth falls below +15% for two consecutive quarters (structural growth break / AP-capex digestion) **OR** the JetStep panel ramp slips past 2027 without converting the two qualified packaging suppliers into volume orders.

→ **CLOSE if** simultaneous: 2026 revenue growth lands below +15% (AP-capex peak confirmed cyclical, not structural) **+** non-GAAP gross margin falls below 53% (pricing power breaking as KLA/Camtek compete in overlapping AP categories) **+** no panel-litho HVM design wins materialize by end-2027 (the optionality is dead). Equivalent: all three differentiated pillars (AP growth, margin, panel optionality) break together.
