## Management and culture

Hypothesis: Weak fit on [[Lens - Management and Culture]]: Gate 1 passes (NAND/HBF/AI-storage is a changeable industry); Gate 2 largely fails after the +5,761% re-rate because cycle and enterprise-NAND optionality already sit in the multiple and the "AI storage pure-play" narrative, with HBF still $0 in the FY30 model. [MC-2] Oct 7 2025 DEF 14A (first standalone; FY26 proxy not filed): CEO/Chair David Goeckeler is the WDC CEO (Mar 2020–Feb 2025) who took the flash spin, not a founder return; 2H FY25 STI formula 139.9% cut to 90% by negative discretion; FY26 STI is profit 50%/FCF 25%/strategy 25% (datacenter share) and LTI is revenue/EPS 50/50, no ROIC; March 2025 launch-grant PSUs hurdle 90-day averages from a $47.07 post-spin base (max $105.91), already spent; combined D&O <1%; Form 4s are 10b5-1 sales, zero clustered buys. [MC-7] July 2026 10-K: ~11,100 employees versus 11,000 in June 2025, three-segment product org. Flash Ventures 49.9% is the execution constraint: Kioxia took XL-Flash, so SNDK cannot force HBF silicon the JV will not vote. §4 calibration is partial: WDC directors Massengill and Alexy were not re-nominated (Nov 2025), Ilkbahar and Shek were promoted to CTO/CLO, Jim Elliott was hired from Samsung DSA as CRO (Jun 2025), NBM rewrote the commercial process; same parent CEO, no headcount purge. [MC-6]/[G-10] entropy base rate is not beaten. Swing variable: the pending FY26 DEF 14A and any open-market insider buys.

## Bull Case
- **HBF creates a new $12B+ market:** Fills the "missing middle" in AI memory hierarchy; SK Hynix partnership + OCP standardization de-risks adoption
- **Structural margin transformation:** 51.1% → 78.4% → 84.6% printed gross margins (83–85% guided Q1 FY27, ~80% modeled FY28–30) are structural (mix shift, CBA, separation from HDD), not cyclical
- **NAND supercycle extension:** HBM capacity diversion, AI demand, sold-out 2026 capacity sustain pricing through 2027
- **Enterprise SSD share inflection:** Stargate program converting hyperscaler quals could step-change Datacenter revenue in 2H 2026
- **Edge AI demand vector:** AI PCs, local inference, context window inflation create net-new NAND demand not in traditional models
- **Jevons Paradox on efficiency gains:** TurboQuant/algorithmic improvements increase total AI adoption → more storage demand
- **Flash Ventures JV:** Cost-plus wafer economics without full fab capex; extended to 2034
- **Forward P/E ~7.8x on FY2027E:** Not expensive if ~$211 consensus EPS holds
- **Bluefield-4 KV-cache-to-NAND independently validates the "NAND as AI memory tier" thesis:** NVIDIA's Bluefield-4 Context Memory Storage Platform (Grace + ConnectX-9) offloads model KV-cache to high-speed NAND, the same "missing middle" HBF targets, reached via NVIDIA's DPU/networking path. A net-new high-performance-NAND demand vector and third-party architectural validation that AI working-memory is migrating into NAND. Per [[Research/2026-06-02 - Datacenter CPU Landscape 2026 - deep-dive]].

## Bear Case
- **Stock up ~5,761% from spin-off:** Limited margin for error even -30% below the July ATH ($2,354)
- **HBF execution risk:** Pre-revenue technology; if sampling is delayed or yields are poor, AI premium evaporates
- **Cycle timing:** Memory supercycles have never sustained beyond 2–3 years; 84.6% gross margins are historically unprecedented in NAND
- **Enterprise SSD share is only 4.1%:** Samsung/Solidigm/Micron have entrenched enterprise relationships; qualification takes 12–18 months
- **No HBM diversification:** 100% NAND exposure; cannot participate in the highest-margin memory segment ($98B HBM TAM by 2030)
- **Samsung competitive response:** If Samsung enters HBF with 10x the R&D budget, SanDisk's first-mover advantage narrows rapidly
- **Customer concentration:** 89% of enterprise revenue from top 7 cloud providers; asymmetric negotiating leverage
- **Algorithmic efficiency compounding:** If TurboQuant + Muon + quantization compound → fewer GPUs per DC → fewer SSDs per rack

## Catalysts
- **Q3 + Q4 FY2026 earnings, cleared:** Q3 (Apr 30) printed $5.95B / 78.4% GM / $23.41 vs $4.4–4.8B guided; Q4 (Aug 5) printed $8.97B / 84.6% / $39.25 and guided Q1 FY2027 to $10.3–10.8B at 83–85% GM; the next make-or-break is the late-October Q1 print delivering that guide
- **~~HBF sampling milestone (H2 2026)~~ → slipped:** first HBF die taped out; customer samples now **2027** ([[Research/2026-08-14 - SNDK - Asymmetrical Bets Investor Day Recap - deep-dive]]). FY30 model still $0 HBF revenue.
- **Stargate hyperscaler qualification conversions:** 3 additional qualifications + top storage OEM expected in calendar 2026
- **NVIDIA Rubin architecture reveal:** If HBF integration is confirmed, validates SanDisk's strategic roadmap
- **Flash Memory Summit 2026:** HBF yield data, competitive landscape updates, BiCS roadmap
- **2027 LTA contract announcements, realized:** NBM contracted book stepped to $93.9B / 10 agreements / ~50% of FY27 bits at the Aug 13 Investor Day; the open question is no longer signing but whether floors hold through a downcycle

## Risks
1. **HBF commercialization failure:** If sampling is delayed, yields are poor, or NVIDIA doesn't adopt, the AI premium in the stock evaporates
2. **Cycle peak and margin reversion:** If NAND pricing reverts to 2023 levels, margins collapse from the mid-80s to single digits; pure NAND exposure amplifies cyclicality

8. **Japanese photo-materials supply chain disruption (new, 2026-04-22):** Iran War Hormuz blockade disrupts Japanese PGME/PGMEA solvent supply → threatens PR/BARC/SOH production at Shin-Etsu/TOK/JSR/Fujifilm consumed by the Flash Ventures JV fabs (Yokkaichi + Kitakami). # [148/159] Theses/SOI - Soitec.md
**thesis · ticker: SOI · status: draft · conviction: medium · sector: Semiconductor Capital Equipment · date: 2026-06-08 · metrics as of: 2026-07-12 · tags: thesis, semiconductors, semiconductor-capital-equipment, engineered-substrates, photonics, RF, SOI · source: FY26 full-year results (May 27, 2026) + Q3'26 release (Feb 3, 2026) + Skyworks/POI agreement (Mar 4, 2026) + NSIG/Simgui 10-year extension (Mar 13, 2026) + CEO transition announcements (Oct 2025 / Jan 2026) + sell-side coverage + sector context**

## Summary

Soitec is two businesses traded as one engineered-substrate company, with sell-side anchored to the wrong half. RF-SOI / Mobile Communications (52% of FY26 revenue, -41% YoY constant currency, Q4 -52% YoY) dominates the framing and drove the FY26 revenue collapse to €592M (-34%), but the underlying story is that Photonics-SOI (>$100M FY26, mgmt guides 20-30% annual growth) is the **sole volume-qualified substrate supplier at all three CPO silicon-photonics foundries** (TSMC COUPE, GlobalFoundries Fotonix, Tower PH18) at the exact moment hyperscale CPO commercialisation begins (TSMC COUPE in risk production with AMD Feb 2026; Broadcom Bailly has shipped 50K+ switches; NVIDIA Quantum-X engines are TSMC COUPE-based). The non-consensus claim is that the market is valuing this near-monopoly substrate position at zero while pricing in a worst-case RF-SOI extension, the inverse of the actual structural setup. Conviction is medium: the Photonics-SOI thesis is real and the moat (qualification across three foundries + 4,300+ Smart Cut patents + 30-year process refinement) is durable; offset by a ~€6.7B market cap at ~11.5x EV/Revenue / ~45x EV/EBITDA on FY26 leaves no margin for the cyclical earnings miss that low FY27 fab loading + FX + lower French CIR funding has already been pre-announced for, and the CEO transition (Barnabé out 31 March 2026, Rémont in 1 April 2026) is a 6-12 month strategy-clarity gap with the formal AGM director vote not until July 2026.

## Key Non-consensus Insights

**1. Soitec is two businesses traded as one, and the market is anchoring to the wrong one.** Sell-side coverage of Soitec is dominated by the RF-SOI / Mobile Communications narrative (52% of FY26 revenue, -41% YoY constant currency, Q4 -52% YoY) and treats Photonics-SOI as upside optionality. The actual structural setup is inverted: Photonics-SOI is the only commercially qualified volume substrate supplier at TSMC COUPE, GlobalFoundries Fotonix, and Tower PH18, the three CPO/silicon-photonics foundries that will ship all hyperscale optical-interconnect volume through 2028. Tower's PH18, GFS's Fotonix, IMEC's iSiPP, and Intel's SiPh platform are all SOI-based with SiN waveguide layers added on top, and the SOI starting material has to be individually qualified at each foundry for specific layer thickness (220nm or 340nm), uniformity (<1nm across the wafer), and defect density (<0.1/cm²). Shin-Etsu holds a Smart Cut license but sells no meaningful volume in photonics-grade SOI; the qualification gap is the moat, not the patent. Management guides 20-30% annual growth on a $100M+ FY26 base, entirely consistent with TSMC COUPE volume ramp 2026-2028, AVGO Bailly's 50K+ shipped switches, and NVIDIA Quantum-X engines (all TSMC COUPE-based). The market valuing this near-monopoly position at zero implies Photonics-SOI will not scale, the opposite of every observable foundry datapoint.

**2. POI is a structurally durable second leg the market is conflating with the RF-SOI cycle.** POI (Piezoelectric-on-Insulator) is to SAW filters what RF-SOI was to PA front-end switches a decade ago: an engineered substrate that fundamentally enables a new generation of high-frequency components. Skyworks signed a multi-year agreement on March 4, 2026 to use Soitec POI wafers for its Sky5 5G platform; Qualcomm has a separate POI HVM agreement; 13 customers are in production and 12 more in testing. Content per phone is structurally rising 4mm² → 11mm² as 5G spectrum crowding intensifies and phones need more sophisticated filtering. Because POI revenue is bundled inside Mobile Communications, it gets pulled down with the RF-SOI inventory correction in sell-side modelling, but the underlying multi-year SAW-filter design-win cycle is independent of smartphone unit volumes and even directionally opposite (more bands per phone, not more phones). The TC-SAW/ML-SAW market is split across Skyworks / Qorvo / Murata / Qualcomm / Broadcom, all of whom either are POI customers or have qualified Soitec material; Soitec captures the substrate layer below the filter-vendor competition.

**3. The Smart Cut royalty stream is a hidden annuity on ~80% of global SOI volume that sell-side does not separately model.** Soitec licenses Smart Cut to Shin-Etsu (1997, renewed 2012) and Simgui / NSIG (2014, 200mm-only); neither license includes new technology transfer or post-license process improvements; both are version-locked at the license date. Licensees produce competing wafers but pay Soitec a royalty per wafer, and ~80% of all SOI wafers shipped globally accrue some royalty stream. The Simgui arrangement was extended for ten more years on March 13, 2026 with **no new tech transfer and a joint commitment to strengthen Soitec's patents in China**, strategically defusing the Chinese substitution risk that bears habitually use to discount the equity. Soitec filed 42 new patents in H1 FY26 alone on a stock of 4,300+ active patents; the IP barrier is being reinforced as a deliberate strategy. The royalty stream is invisible in segment disclosure but represents a durable annuity on the architecture, not the wafer.

**4. The market is mispricing the CEO transition as continuity risk when Rémont's RF/sensor/auto/AI background signals the opposite.** Pierre Barnabé (ex-Atos, ex-Bull, ex-Crédit Lyonnais) was parachuted in 2022 as a financial/operational fixer to manage the RF-SOI cycle. Laurent Rémont (appointed January 8, 2026, advisor from March 16, CEO effective April 1, board-director vote at the July 2026 AGM) is Infineon SVP, with prior roles at Kontron and STMicroelectronics, all in RF / sensors / automotive / AI. His background maps precisely onto Soitec's diversification end-markets (RF-SOI / POI for mobile, FD-SOI for auto-AI, SmartSiC for ST power, Photonics-SOI for AI datacom). The advisor-onboarding before formal handoff implies strategy continuity and likely an explicit board mandate to accelerate the diversification away from RF-SOI single-cycle exposure, exactly the analyst bear thesis. Market is treating the transition as ambiguity discount; the better read is that the board picked a technical / end-market specialist rather than another financial fixer because the cycle work is done and the strategic ramp execution is the next phase.

**5. The scrapped $2B revenue / 40% EBITDA medium-term targets are a tactical narrative reset, not a strategic capitulation.** Bears read the FY26 scrapping of guidance (both formal FY26 outlook and the medium-term $2B / 40% EBITDA target) as management losing confidence. The opposite read is that management chose to remove a public anchor that the RF-SOI cycle had already disproved (RF-SOI alone could never have hit $2B), and quarterly-only guidance gives the new CEO room to reset on the back of Photonics-SOI ramp without the optical baggage of the prior frame. The pattern is closely analogous to Lisa Su scrapping Read Rory's PC-volume targets at AMD in 2014-2015 and resetting on data center; the credibility came from the segment-mix shift, not the absolute numbers. If Rémont uses the July 2026 AGM and the Q1'27 print (likely late July / early August) to anchor a new revenue mix framework foregrounding Photonics-SOI and POI, the narrative reset becomes a re-rating catalyst rather than a discount.

## Outstanding Questions

**1. What is the actual unit and revenue trajectory of Photonics-SOI through FY27-FY28, and does the 20-30% CAGR management guidance under-shoot or over-shoot the CPO ramp?** Photonics-SOI revenue >$100M in FY26 against management guide of 20-30% CAGR implies ~$120-130M FY27 and ~$150-170M FY28; these numbers do not embed full hyperscale CPO commercialisation pull-through. AVGO Bailly has shipped 50K+ Tomahawk switches with CPO; NVIDIA Quantum-X / Spectrum-X use TSMC COUPE engines; AMD is at risk production. Each photonic die requires Photonics-SOI starting material with the unique foundry-specific qualification spec. Resolution: Q1'27 print Photonics-SOI segment disclosure; H1 FY27 customer breakdown if disclosed.

**2. Does POI revenue cross 15-20% of Mobile Communications by FY28, or does it remain trapped under the RF-SOI inventory cycle in the segment lines?** POI customer count (13 production + 12 testing) implies a 1-2 year ramp to broad adoption. If Soitec separately discloses POI revenue in any FY27 or FY28 quarterly print, sell-side has a forced reframing trigger. If POI stays buried inside Mobile and never breaks out, the market continues conflating it with RF-SOI weakness. Resolution: Skyworks Sky5 production ramp commentary (Skyworks FY27 quarterly transcripts); any Soitec segment-disclosure change at H1 FY27 or FY27 full-year.

**3. When does the RF-SOI Mobile cycle actually bottom: H1 FY27, H2 FY27, or FY28?** Q4 FY26 mobile was -52% YoY. Customer inventory remains "high" per Soitec language. Smartphone unit volumes are in their second consecutive year of contraction; 5G slot growth is the offsetting demand variable. If RF-SOI Mobile is still -25% YoY in H2 FY27, the cyclical bottom is past calendar 2027, and the multi-year FCF profile compresses materially. Resolution: Skyworks / Qorvo / Murata quarterly transcripts on RF front-end inventory; Apple iPhone 18 cycle volumes (Sep 2026 launch).

**4. What is the realistic SmartSiC volume timeline at STMicroelectronics, and does ST commit to 200mm SmartSiC at scale or hedge to Wolfspeed / Coherent / SK Siltron CSS?** Soitec announced ST SmartSiC qualification cooperation September 2023 with an 18-month timeline (completion ~early 2025) and volume production "midterm". Auto & Industrial revenue -44% YoY in FY26 implies SmartSiC is not yet a meaningful contributor; ST's own SiC strategy is under cost pressure from Wolfspeed bankruptcy-era dumping and SK Siltron CSS / Resonac competition. If ST defers SmartSiC volume to FY28 or beyond, one of Soitec's three diversification legs is delayed. Resolution: ST quarterly capex and SiC commentary; any ST formal SmartSiC PO disclosure.

**5. What is Rémont's strategic intent at the July 2026 AGM, and does he reset the medium-term financial framework or maintain the quarterly-only guidance posture?** The medium-term $2B / 40% EBITDA target was scrapped. A new framework anchored to Photonics-SOI mix shift (e.g., "Photonics-SOI to 30%+ of revenue by FY30 at >50% incremental margin") would be a re-rating catalyst. Continued quarterly-only guidance under a new CEO would be read as residual uncertainty about the cycle and would maintain the analyst dispersion (PT range €26-250).

**6. Does the Simgui / NSIG ten-year extension hold against Chinese government pressure for independent domestic substitution?** The March 13, 2026 extension is explicit about no new technology transfer, joint patent strengthening, and Soitec retaining worldwide sales rights, the strongest possible defensive structure for an upstream substrate position in China. But geopolitical pressure has overridden similar commercial arrangements (Beijing's domestic substitution mandate has displaced ASML DUV, Lam etch, etc., despite contracts). Soitec's IP density (4,300+ patents, NSIG joint commitment) is uniquely positioned vs. ASML's EUV: substrate IP is less amenable to clean-room substitution, but the risk is non-zero on a 10-year horizon.

**7. Why is sell-side dispersion (PT range €26-250, 6 Buy / 10 Hold / 2 Sell) so extreme, and what single datapoint forces convergence?** A €26 low PT implies the analyst is modelling a permanent RF-SOI structural decline; a €250 high PT implies full-credit for Photonics-SOI + POI + SmartSiC ramps without execution risk. The dispersion signals the market has not chosen between the two business framings. Q1'27 print is the most likely convergence event: Photonics-SOI revenue line + RF-SOI sequential trajectory together force a directional reframing.

**8. How does the position size, given that Soitec sits at the picks-and-shovels chokepoint for the photonics demand cycle but at a substantially less-discounted multiple than other vault picks-and-shovels names?** Compared with [[Theses/IQE - IQE]] (III-V substrate, ~6x EV/Revenue, M&A special-situation overlay), [[Theses/AIXA - Aixtron]] (MOCVD, semicap equipment-cycle multiple), [[Theses/AEHR - Aehr Test Systems]] (wafer-level burn-in, ~5-7x EV/Revenue at run-rate), and [[Theses/FORM - FormFactor]] (probe cards, ~3x EV/Revenue), Soitec at ~11.5x EV/Revenue / ~45x EV/EBITDA is the **most expensive** of the photonics picks-and-shovels basket. Position sizing should reflect this: entry at 50-100bp on cyclical bottoming, scaled to 1.5-2% only on confirmed Photonics-SOI ramp velocity.

## Business Model & Product Description

Soitec is the dominant global manufacturer of **engineered substrates**: semiconductor wafers that are not standard bulk silicon, indium-phosphide, or silicon-carbide but custom-built structures (typically a thin top device layer bonded to a different bulk handle wafer with an intervening insulating layer) that enable specific device performance characteristics no monolithic substrate can deliver. The core enabling technology is **Smart Cut™**, a proprietary process invented at France's CEA-Leti in the 1990s and exclusively licensed to Soitec: hydrogen ion implantation into a donor wafer at a precise depth, bonding the donor to a handle wafer, and thermally splitting off a thin (typically 60-340 nm) device layer that remains attached to the handle wafer with the implanted oxide between them. The result is a wafer with the surface electrical properties of the donor and the mechanical / thermal / cost properties of the handle. Soitec holds 4,300+ active patents on Smart Cut and its derivative process variants, filed 42 new patents in H1 FY26 alone, and licenses the technology to Shin-Etsu (1997, renewed 2012) and Simgui / NSIG (2014, extended 10 years March 2026); together ~80% of global SOI wafer shipments use Smart Cut and pay Soitec a royalty.

**Analogy**: Soitec is to engineered substrates what ASML is to EUV lithography: a single-vendor process-architecture monopoly with a long IP / qualification / customer-relationship moat. The difference is that ASML sells equipment at €200M+ per system to ten foundries; Soitec sells wafers at $50-1000+ per wafer to dozens of customers depending on product, with annual unit volumes in the millions and revenue concentration much lower than ASML's customer mix.

### Management (post-April 1, 2026)

Prior: Infineon SVP, Kontron, STMicroelectronics. Background: RF, sensors, automotive, AI; maps precisely to Soitec's diversification end-markets.
- **Outgoing CEO**: Pierre Barnabé (2022 - March 31, 2026). Prior: Atos, Bull, Crédit Lyonnais. Profile: financial / operational fixer; departed after navigating the RF-SOI down-cycle.

## Industry Context

**Where Soitec sits in the semiconductor value chain**: Engineered substrates occupy a niche between the standard wafer suppliers (Shin-Etsu, SUMCO, GlobalWafers, Siltronic, SK Siltron; combined >90% of bulk 300mm silicon) and the foundries (TSMC, Samsung, GlobalFoundries, Intel, Tower, UMC, SMIC). For specific applications (RF where insulator-isolation reduces loss; FD-SOI where the buried oxide enables sub-1V operation; silicon photonics where the buried oxide is the optical cladding; SiC where engineered substrates dodge the bulk-SiC defect-density wall) engineered substrates are mandatory and the standard wafer cannot substitute. Soitec is the only company with a broad portfolio across all engineered substrate types (RF-SOI, FD-SOI, Photonics-SOI, POI, Imager-SOI, SmartSiC). Competition is product-specific rather than company-specific.

### Competitive landscape by product line

| Product | Soitec position | Key competitors | Moat |
|---|---|---|---|
| **RF-SOI** | ~38% global SOI share leader | Shin-Etsu (21.7%, Smart Cut licensee, version-locked at 2012); GlobalWafers; SMIC RF-SOI (internal Chinese substitution); Simgui (Soitec-licensed manufacturing for China market only) | Qualification + customer relationships + Smart Cut process control |
| **POI** | Sole qualified volume vendor | None at production scale; Murata internal SAW substrate (different architecture); Chinese filter makers using non-POI bulk piezoelectric | First-mover qualification + 13 production + 12 testing customer relationships |
| **FD-SOI** | Sole supplier to GlobalFoundries 22FDX | Shin-Etsu (Smart Cut license but no meaningful FD-SOI volume); Samsung 28nm FD-SOI internal | Exclusive GFS partnership |
| **Photonics-SOI** | **Near-monopoly**: sole qualified volume vendor at TSMC, GFS, Tower, Intel, IMEC | Shin-Etsu (holds Smart Cut license, sells no meaningful volume); no other qualified vendor at production scale | Foundry qualification specifications (220nm / 340nm layer, <1nm uniformity, <0.1/cm² defect density); unique per foundry, 12-18 months to re-qualify a second vendor |
| **SmartSiC** | Sole 200mm SmartSiC architecture | Wolfspeed (bulk 200mm SiC), Coherent (bulk SiC), SK Siltron CSS, Resonac, Showa Denko | Pre-volume; architecture advantage (donor wafer reusable, lower CapEx per wafer) but unproven at HVM |
| **Smart Cut royalty** | 100% (sole licensor) | n/a | 4,300+ patents; Shin-Etsu and Simgui licensees version-locked; 42 new patents H1 FY26 |

### Pricing power dynamics

Pricing power is asymmetric across the product portfolio:
- **Highest in Photonics-SOI**: monopoly + custom foundry qualification + small unit-volume / high-ASP profile. Photonics-SOI wafers reportedly run $500-1000+ per wafer vs. standard 300mm SOI ~$200-300. Margin profile is closest to ASML-like in the semicap ecosystem.
- **High in POI**: sole qualified vendor at scale; multi-year design-in cycles create switching cost; Skyworks and Qualcomm multi-year agreements lock pricing visibility.
- **Moderate in RF-SOI**: dominant share but Shin-Etsu and Simgui licensees compete; smartphone OEM oligopoly (Apple, Samsung, Huawei, Xiaomi, OPPO) has annual ASP negotiation leverage; Chinese internal substitution at SMIC compresses long-term pricing.
- **Moderate in FD-SOI**: dependent on GlobalFoundries 22FDX volume cycle; GFS pricing leverage caps Soitec margin.
- **Pre-volume in SmartSiC**: pricing TBD at ST qualification; SiC bulk substrate ASPs are under pressure from Wolfspeed bankruptcy-era inventory dumping.
- **Royalty annuity stream**: durable, low-touch, ~80% of global SOI volume; structural margin >90%.

### Structural forces reshaping the engineered-substrate market

**1. Silicon photonics commercialisation at hyperscale (2026-2030)**. TSMC COUPE in risk production with AMD (Feb 2026); AVGO Bailly with 50K+ shipped switches; NVIDIA Quantum-X / Spectrum-X with TSMC COUPE engines; Marvell-Celestial AI Photonic Fabric. Each photonic die requires Photonics-SOI starting material; foundries cannot substitute with bulk silicon (no buried oxide → no optical confinement). Cross-reference: [[Sectors/Photonic Metrology]] §Macro shifts: 1.6T module volumes 2.5M → 20M units 2025→2026 (Nomura); SiPh share of high-end transceivers 50-70% 2026 (TrendForce).

**2. 5G mid-band density driving POI substrate growth**. POI content per smartphone rising 4mm² → 11mm² as 5G spectrum allocation expands and filter selectivity requirements tighten. POI adoption ramps even if smartphone unit volumes are flat: the architecture is volume-multiplicative, not unit-cycle-correlated. Skyworks Mar 2026 Sky5 deal is the bellwether; Qualcomm in HVM; Murata, Qorvo, Broadcom all qualified or qualifying.

**3. SiC 150mm → 200mm cost-leverage transition**. SiC bulk substrate cost has fallen from $1500 (2020) to $700 (2025) for 150mm; the 200mm transition compresses unit cost another 50%. SmartSiC's donor-reuse architecture should be cost-advantaged vs. bulk SiC at 200mm but requires production-scale validation at STMicro. Cross-reference: [[Sectors/MLCC & Power Semiconductors.md]] for SiC value-chain context.

**4. Chinese substitution pressure on commodity SOI**. SMIC has internal RF-SOI capability; Chinese foundries are under government mandate to source domestically. The Simgui ten-year extension (March 2026) is the defensive structure: Soitec licenses the manufacturing rather than ceding the IP. Effectiveness vs. Beijing's broader substitution drive is the open question (See [[Theses/SOI - Soitec.md#Outstanding Questions]] #6).

**5. Edge AI driving FD-SOI revival**. GlobalFoundries 22FDX+ launched late 2023 with embedded AI accelerators for IoT edge; Soitec FD-SOI wafer capacity expanded 40% early 2024 specifically for industrial / automotive Edge AI ramp. 22FDX has 50+ designs across automotive, 5G connectivity, IoT. The FD-SOI revival is real but small (~€110-130M FY26 vs. €592M total); thesis upside requires FD-SOI to step-function up if hyperscaler captive accelerators move some volume to FDX-class processes.

### Where Soitec sits versus the photonics picks-and-shovels basket

| Vault picks-and-shovels thesis | Layer | EV/Revenue (FY26) | Sector |
|---|---|---|---|
| [[Theses/IQE - IQE]] | III-V epi substrate | ~6x | Optical Networking & Photonics |
| [[Theses/AIXA - Aixtron]] | MOCVD reactor (III-V epi tool) | ~3-4x | Semiconductor Capital Equipment |
| [[Theses/AEHR - Aehr Test Systems]] | Wafer-level burn-in | ~5-7x (run-rate) | Semiconductor Capital Equipment |
| [[Theses/FORM - FormFactor]] | Probe cards (optical + electrical) | ~3x | Semiconductor Capital Equipment |
| [[Theses/BESI - BE Semiconductor Industries]] | Hybrid bonding | ~10x | Semiconductor Capital Equipment |
| **Soitec (SOI)** | **Engineered substrate (SOI + Photonics-SOI + POI + FD-SOI + SmartSiC)** | **~11.5x** | **Semiconductor Capital Equipment** |
| [[Theses/LITE - Lumentum]] | Laser / EML / SiPh modules | ~12-15x | Optical Networking & Photonics |

Soitec sits at the **upstream substrate layer**, the closest demand-side analog to LITE/COHR at modules (not at picks-and-shovels equipment-cycle multiples). The position is two layers above the foundry (substrate → foundry → module → system); pricing power and durability are intermediate between AIXA's equipment-cycle pure picks-and-shovels and LITE's module-cycle thesis-cycle multiple.

See [[Sectors/Semiconductor Capital Equipment]] for parent-sector context and [[Sectors/Photonic Metrology]] for the downstream test sub-cluster perspective on the same demand cycle.

## Management and culture

Hypothesis: Weak fit on [[Lens - Management and Culture]]. Gate 1 passes (Photonics-SOI, POI, SmartSiC at CPO / 5G-filter / 200mm-SiC inflections); Gate 2 residual because 6 Buy / 10 Hold / 2 Sell and €26–250 PTs still treat Photonics as optionality on RF-SOI, even after Q1'27 Photonics sales doubling. [MC-2] FY27 STI (AGM 29 July 2026, all resolutions >98%): 20% Photonics revenue, 20% current EBIT, 20% FCF, the product-volume metric the lens wants, against LTI 40% relative TSR / 35% EPS, a 10%-of-fixed hold on €500k salary, and ~0.04% CEO ownership (8,012 Onyx 28 sign-on + 7,015 Onyx 29 PS). No founder; Bpifrance 11.45% / 16.91% votes plus CEA 7.19% / 11.25% votes is a loyalty-share state-adjacent block. FY26 STI paid 83.6% (€443k) with 0% on revenue and 0% on EBITDA; the diversification kicker scored 0%. [MC-7] product org at 2,128 headcount (2,252 → 2,128 FY25–FY26); CPO René Jonker from October 2025. [MC-6] six-month APLD furlough at Bernin from mid-November 2025 (~1,800) plus a 5% two-month "solidarity" cut is cost-cycle management, not an entropy-fighting mechanism. 21–22 November 2025 director buys (Barnabé 854 @ €23.48, Gegout 1,500 @ €22.75) are sub-€35k; FSP sold 299,863 shares 20–22 April 2026. Swing variable: whether Photonics-weighted STI plus the CPO org convert CRAs and Singapore 300mm qualification before FY26 bonus-padding repeats.

## Bull Case

The bull case is a Photonics-SOI-led re-rating coupled with a cyclical RF-SOI / Auto recovery.

**Mechanism**: Photonics-SOI ramps to $200-300M revenue by FY28 on hyperscale CPO commercialisation (TSMC COUPE volume + AVGO Bailly expansion + NVIDIA Quantum-X engines), pulling group revenue from €592M FY26 → €750-900M FY28. POI scales with Skyworks Sky5 production ramp and Qualcomm HVM growth; Mobile Communications recovers to €400-450M by FY28 (mid-cycle, not peak). FD-SOI + Photonics-SOI Edge & Cloud AI segment compounds at 20-25% to €350-400M by FY28. SmartSiC begins meaningful ST volume contribution in H2 FY27 / FY28, adding €40-60M to Auto & Industrial. Smart Cut royalty stream grows ~10% per year as global SOI volume expands with photonics ramp. Total group revenue €900M-€1.1B FY28 at 30-32% EBITDA margin = €270-350M EBITDA. At a 25-30x EV/EBITDA multiple (consistent with a structurally-growing pure-play picks-and-shovels at a recovering cycle), equity value €7-10B = €155-220/share at current ~46.5M share count.

**Specific drivers**:
1. Photonics-SOI revenue line breaks out in Q1'27 or H1 FY27 with >35% YoY growth (vs 20-30% guide); forces sell-side reframe
2. POI design-win disclosure in any FY27 quarter: Soitec separately discloses POI revenue mix inside Mobile
3. Rémont AGM (July 2026) communication anchors a new medium-term framework with Photonics-SOI as the growth driver
4. STMicro SmartSiC formal PO disclosure for FY27 200mm volume
5. RF-SOI Mobile YoY decline narrows to -15% or better in H1 FY27; cyclical bottom confirmed
6. NVIDIA, AVGO, or hyperscaler announces multi-year Photonics-SOI capacity commitment (€100M+); would validate the monopoly framing

**Valuation framework**: €7-10B equity / 46.5M shares = €150-215/share. Current €146.65. Implies ~0-50% upside on bull case execution by FY28; downside protection via cash flow generation and royalty annuity.

## Bear Case

The bear case is cycle-extension coupled with multiple compression on the Photonics-SOI optionality.

**Mechanism (cycle)**: RF-SOI inventory correction extends into FY28 (smartphone unit volumes contract for third year; OEM destocking persists). FD-SOI revenue stalls as GlobalFoundries' 22FDX cycle plateaus and Samsung 28nm FD-SOI captures incremental design-ins. SmartSiC at STMicro is qualified but ST defers volume to Wolfspeed bankruptcy-era dumped inventory and SK Siltron CSS / Resonac lower-cost alternatives. SmartSiC FY28 revenue stays under €30M. POI ramps but slower than Skyworks / Qualcomm public framing implies: Chinese filter makers (Murata, etc., not Chinese-owned but with China manufacturing) adopt POI selectively, capping volume. Photonics-SOI grows to $150M by FY28 vs. management 20-30% guide, meaningful but not transformative. Group revenue €650-700M FY28 at 20-22% EBITDA margin = €130-155M EBITDA. At a compressed 15-18x EV/EBITDA multiple (sell-side stops awarding Photonics-SOI premium), equity value €2-2.8B = €43-60/share, 60-70% downside.

**Mechanism (competitive)**: Shin-Etsu activates dormant Smart Cut license for photonics-grade SOI and qualifies at GFS or Tower (technically possible: Shin-Etsu has the license, just no current photonics-grade volume). Soitec's Photonics-SOI monopoly compresses to 50-60% share; pricing power compresses correspondingly. Or: Chinese government accelerates substrate substitution mandate, NSIG / Simgui or a new Chinese vendor brings 300mm SOI to volume despite license restrictions; Soitec's China revenue contribution (likely 15-25% of total) compresses.

**What does the world look like where this loses money**: Q1'27 (July-August 2026) print reveals Photonics-SOI growth at 15% YoY or lower (vs 20-30% guide), AND Mobile Communications down >35% YoY, AND Rémont gives a tactical / cyclical commentary without anchoring a new strategic framework. The stock retraces to €60-80 in the following two quarters (sell-side downgrades; momentum reversal from +545% off-bottom rally). Multi-year story is reset.

**Specific risks driving the bear**:
1. RF-SOI cycle extends 12-18 months beyond bull-case bottoming assumption
2. Photonics-SOI second supplier emerges (Shin-Etsu activation, or new Chinese entrant)
3. SmartSiC volume slips at ST or ST commercially deprioritises engineered SiC architecture
4. CEO transition execution risk (Rémont integration takes 6-12 months; strategy reset delayed)
5. French CIR (research tax credit) further restricted under fiscal-consolidation pressure (FY27 funding headwind already pre-announced)
6. Chinese substrate substitution accelerates outside the Simgui arrangement

## Catalysts

**Near-term (next 6 months)**:
- **Q1'27 print (late July / early August 2026)**: first quarterly under Rémont; Photonics-SOI growth disclosure (vs 20-30% CAGR guide); Mobile Communications sequential trajectory; any segment-mix reset. Highest-information event of the next 12 months.
- **AGM July 2026**: formal Rémont director vote; strategic outlook commentary; potential new medium-term framework or continued quarterly-only guidance posture.
- **Skyworks Q4 FY26 / Q1 FY27 transcript (Aug-Nov 2026)**: Sky5 production ramp commentary; POI volume reference (Skyworks is unlikely to name Soitec but volume signals are extractable).
- **TSMC COUPE volume ramp commentary**: TSMC quarterly capex + advanced packaging commentary (Apr, Jul, Oct, Jan reports); pulls Photonics-SOI demand.

**Medium-term (6-18 months)**:
- **H1 FY27 results (November 2026)**: first complete half-year under Rémont; FY27 trajectory clarification.
- **STMicro FY26 results + 2027 guidance (January-February 2027)**: SmartSiC commentary; any volume PO disclosure.
- **CES 2027 + MWC 2027**: 5G filter / RF / edge AI ecosystem signals.
- **FY27 full-year results (May 2027)**: segment trajectory; Photonics-SOI revenue line if broken out.

**Long-term (12-36 months)**:
- **Hyperscale CPO commercial deployment at scale (2027-2028)**: directly pulls Photonics-SOI demand.
- **NVIDIA Rubin Ultra / AMD MI400 generation**: increased per-die test/burn-in requirements; substrate qualification carries through.
- **SmartSiC at ST volume production**: if it lands FY28, becomes meaningful Auto & Industrial segment driver.

**Negative catalysts**:
- **Shin-Etsu photonics-grade SOI announcement**: would break the Photonics-SOI monopoly framing immediately even if 12-18 months from production
- **STMicro defers SmartSiC volume PO**: invalidates one of the three diversification legs
- **Q1'27 Photonics-SOI growth <15% YoY**: undermines mgmt 20-30% guide credibility
- **CEO transition disruption**: any high-profile executive departure during Rémont integration

## Risks

**Thesis risks (investment case is wrong)**:

1. **Photonics-SOI growth comes in materially below mgmt 20-30% CAGR guide**. The thesis hinges on Photonics-SOI being the structural growth driver; sub-20% growth means the monopoly is not being monetised at the rate implied by the foundry-qualification position, and the bull-case mix shift is delayed.

2. **Shin-Etsu activates dormant Smart Cut license for photonics-grade SOI**. Shin-Etsu has held the license since 1997 and could in principle qualify a photonics-grade product at GFS or Tower. The qualification gap is 12-18 months, not insurmountable. A formal Shin-Etsu announcement would compress the Photonics-SOI monopoly framing immediately.

3. **RF-SOI inventory correction extends into FY28**. Smartphone unit volumes have contracted for two consecutive years; if the third consecutive year materialises (per the Yole / Counterpoint bear case for 2026-2027), Mobile Communications revenue could be flat to down again in FY27, pushing the cycle bottom to FY28 and compressing the multi-year FCF trajectory.

4. **SmartSiC stalls at STMicro**. The Sep 2023 qualification cooperation should have delivered volume production by H1 FY26 per original 18-month timeline; the absence of meaningful Auto & Industrial revenue suggests ST is deferring. If ST formally walks (commercial deprioritisation in favour of Wolfspeed inventory or SK Siltron CSS), one of three diversification legs evaporates.

5. **POI commoditisation if Shin-Etsu or Chinese filter makers vertically integrate the substrate**. POI is currently a sole-qualified architecture, but the moat is qualification + customer relationships, not exotic physics. A Murata-internal or Skyworks-internal POI program (or a Chinese substitute) would compress Soitec's pricing power.

**Position risks (thesis right, stock down)**:

6. **Multi-compression on macro / rates**. ~45x EV/EBITDA on FY26 is sensitive to discount-rate moves; 100bp rate move can compress 20-25% on multiple alone even with bookings unchanged.

7. **CEO transition execution risk**. Rémont integration period (6-12 months); any strategy ambiguity, executive departure, or guidance miss in the first three Rémont prints (Q1 FY27, H1 FY27, FY27 full-year) creates volatility.

8. **Sell-side dispersion realisation**. PT range €26-250 implies extreme analyst disagreement. Either side of the disagreement realising in a single report can cause 10-20% daily moves (the +545% from Nov 2025 trough is the existence proof).

9. **French CIR (research tax credit) funding pressure**. Management explicitly flagged "lower funding" as FY27 profitability headwind. Further French fiscal-consolidation measures could compound this.

10. **Equity supply event**. After +545% rally, secondary issuance, insider sales, or convertible refinancing at premium valuation is a non-zero risk, particularly given French government holding via Bpifrance and CEA.

## Conviction Triggers

**→ HIGH if**: Q1'27 (Jul-Aug 2026) discloses Photonics-SOI growth >35% YoY (vs 20-30% guide) AND RF-SOI Mobile YoY decline narrows to <-20% (vs -41% FY26) AND Rémont AGM (July 2026) anchors new medium-term Photonics-SOI mix-shift framework. Three-condition gate validates Photonics-SOI ramp velocity, cyclical bottom passing, and strategic continuity.

**→ HIGH if**: Soitec announces formal multi-year Photonics-SOI capacity commitment with a named hyperscale customer (NVDA, AVGO, GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN) ≥$50M; would force sell-side to price the monopoly explicitly.

**→ LOW if**: Q1'27 reveals Photonics-SOI growth <15% YoY (below the mgmt guide floor) AND RF-SOI Mobile continues at -40% or worse; signals the bull-case timeline is broken on both legs simultaneously.

**→ LOW if**: Shin-Etsu publicly qualifies photonics-grade SOI at GlobalFoundries or Tower Semiconductor: breaks the monopoly narrative; would compress the Photonics-SOI valuation premium even ahead of any volume impact.

**→ CLOSE if**: STMicroelectronics announces SmartSiC qualification delay >12 months OR ST commercially deprioritises SmartSiC in favour of bulk-SiC alternatives; combined with Photonics-SOI growth missing the 20-30% guide for 2 consecutive quarters, would invalidate the diversification thesis at the segment level.

**→ CLOSE if**: Market cap reaches €10B+ (~€215+/share) without commensurate revenue / EBITDA ramp; pure multiple expansion on optionality becomes uninvestable for a substrate company with a one-year revenue cycle visible.

**thesis · ticker: SPCX · status: active · conviction: medium · sector: Neoclouds & GPU-as-a-Service · date: 2026-08-13 · metrics as of: 2026-08-15 · tags: thesis, neoclouds, SPCX · source: SpaceX Q2 2026 8-K/10-Q + earnings call; vault research (Shanaka capital-recovery clock, PhotonCap first-earnings reframe, SemiAnalysis 10GW, Terafab filings, Reddit workplace synthesis); web sweep 2026-08-13. Rebuild of superseded panel file (batch thesis-SPCX-2026-08-13-124943).**

## Summary
SPCX at ~$140 is two capital pools consolidated into one Class A residual: a **proven, owned Connectivity annuity** (Starlink: $4.291B Q2 revenue, 60.5% adj. EBITDA margin, 12.0M subs, riding Falcon's launch-cost monopoly, 73% of group adj. EBITDA) and an **unproven AI capital-recovery bet** ($15.828B of $18.369B Q2 capex against $2.561B AI revenue, a $(1.257)B operating loss, and Cloud Service Agreements terminable on 90 days' notice post-ramp). Sell-side prices the second pool as if proven (avg PT ~$232, range $62–$800, MS $300 on the SemiAnalysis 10 GW / MSFT-largest-offtaker path), while the printed record supports only 1.4 GW nameplate, a ~2 GW YE26 company target, and $14.1B of contracted sales counted under a non-cancellable-window definition that covers 89% of a single quarter's AI build. The mispriced variable is **contract duration versus GPU/turbine depreciation lives**, not GW count. Conviction medium: Connectivity cash, net cash ~$60.6B, and printed anchor tenants (Anthropic bought out all of Colossus 1; Google, Reflection followed) keep it off low; unproven AI ROIC, the widest large-cap valuation dispersion on the board ($63 Morningstar FV to $800 high), and cancellable paper keep it off high.

## Key Non-consensus Insights

- **The listed equity's proven asset is a Connectivity annuity, not an AI compounder**
  - **Consensus:** Sell-side (Buy consensus, avg PT ~$232, MS $300) and the post-IPO tape read Q2 ($7.814B revenue +92%, $3.538B adj. EBITDA) as an AI-infrastructure compounder's first print (the PhotonCap reframe).
  - **Variant:** Segment math says the durable engine is Connectivity: $2.597B of $3.538B group adj. EBITDA (73%) at a 60.5% margin, 38.6% operating margin, enterprise/gov already 42.1% of mix with >$6B multi-year Starshield awards. AI's $1.146B "adj. EBITDA" is a D&A/SBC addback sitting on a $(1.257)B operating loss; Space is a shipping department (38 launches, 28 internal) that loses $(542)M at the operating line while feeding the constellation. What survives a failed AI ROIC is Starlink + Falcon, a vertically-owned annuity no neocloud peer has.
  - **First confirming observable [2026-11]:** Q3 Connectivity adj. EBITDA margin holds ~60% with ARPU lifting after the 18-June price hike (consumer +$5–10, Standby $5→$10, aviation up to +100%) without a churn break.
  - **Breaks if:** Connectivity adj. EBITDA breaks out of the ~60% band on churn/ARPU, the same condition as → LOW.

- **Demand is printed; capital recovery is not, and the landlord competes with its own tenants**
  - **Consensus:** $14.1B contracted Cloud Services sales (+$6.7B early Q3), Anthropic buying out all of Colossus 1, Google and Reflection AI leases, and SemiAnalysis ~$100B/GW/yr ARR framing make the AI build a covered-offtake story.
  - **Variant:** Note 2 counts only the non-cancellable enforceable window under 90-day post-ramp termination rights: $14.1B is 89% of ONE quarter's $15.828B AI capex, against non-cancellable NVDA/HBM/turbine/optics POs upstream. Worse, the tenant base is SPCX's own competition: Anthropic and Google rent Colossus capacity while competing with Grok (and now Cursor) at the application layer, a structural incentive to multi-source and exit the moment alternative capacity exists, which Meta's entry into excess-compute resale is already creating. SPCX carries the shortest-duration paper in the neocloud category (CRWV/NBIS sign multi-year take-or-pay) offset by the strongest balance sheet ($100B cash, IG notes at 5.855% wtd, interest a single-digit % of revenue vs CRWV's 25.8% break-line breach).
  - **First confirming observable [2026-11]:** matched-cohort payback disclosure, or a CSA amendment to long-duration non-cancellable (duration > D&A life), in the Q3 filing.
  - **Breaks if:** first CSA termination cascade (→ LOW); D&A lives < 90-day exits with no Connectivity residual (→ CLOSE).

- **The "Musk repeats the Starlink playbook in AI" transfer inverts the ownership structure that made Starlink work**
  - **Consensus:** The firm that collapsed launch cost and internalized the resulting demand (Starlink) will repeat the move in AI compute: SemiAnalysis's 10 GW by 2027, ~$500B ARR, Microsoft-as-largest-offtaker.
  - **Variant:** Starlink internalized Jevons because SpaceX owned the scarce complement (Falcon; 28 of 38 Q2 launches were internal constellation builds). The AI campus rents every scarce layer (Rubin-exclusive silicon from NVDA, HBM, optics, gas turbines it has agreed to remove from Memphis by 2027) and sells the output on cancellable paper. The MSFT anchor remains unverified: the rumored 3 GW Azure lease has no public confirmation from either party; printed tenants are Anthropic/Google/Reflection. Starlink's 2026 lead does not even need Starship. Flight 13 (24 July) deployed 20 production V3 sats (1 Tbps downlink each) on a suborbital test profile that burned them up by design; Falcon carries the constellation math.
  - **First confirming observable [2027-03]:** a disclosed GW-scale hyperscaler CSA on 2026–27 MW with duration beyond 90-day post-ramp, the one print that would make the Azure-substitute narrative load-bearing.
  - **Breaks if:** YE26 nameplate <2 GW on the same definition as the printed 1.4 GW (→ LOW).

- **A $63-to-$800 valuation dispersion means the market has not agreed what this company is; the variable that collapses it is disclosure, not execution**
  - **Consensus:** There is no consensus; that is the point. Morningstar FV ~$63/sh, Tilson "overvalued by $1T+", CFRA "almost comical growth" needed, vs MS $300 and an $800 high; a $121-wide 52-week range ($104.83–$225.64) in a two-month-old listing; the Aug 6 911M-share unlock absorbed +6% on the day.
  - **Variant:** With dispersion this wide, flow and narrative set the marginal price (lock-up tranches to Dec, ~40% tradeable by year-end; retail momentum), and the single operating disclosure that would collapse the dispersion (CSA duration/cohort payback) is absent from both bull and bear models. Position for the disclosure, not the GW headline: 10 GW / $100B-per-GW / Terafab IDM ($16.8B initial Grimes County filing, up to $119B four-phase, off-grid claim resting on tax-abatement language) are not load-bearing and should be priced at option value until tool POs and named counterparties print.
  - **First confirming observable [2026-12]:** YE26 nameplate ≥2 GW on the 1.4 GW definition, or any duration/payback disclosure in Q3/Q4 filings.
  - **Breaks if:** capital-recovery clock fails (D&A lives < 90-day exits) with no Connectivity residual (→ CLOSE).

## Outstanding Questions

- **CSA duration vs the capital-recovery clock.** Note 2's $14.1B is the non-cancellable window, not headline deal size. What is matched-cohort payback: months of non-cancellable revenue per MW versus GPU/turbine D&A lives (AI D&A already $1.885B in Q2)? Shanaka's paid half (contractual exit architecture, concentration table, $100B December claim bridge, 2027 $22.244B commitment wall) is not ingested. Answered by: cohort disclosure, long-duration CSA amendment, or a termination cascade.
- **YE26 nameplate definition.** 1.4 GW printed (from 1.0 GW Q1, 0.4 GW Q2'25); Musk's ~2 GW YE26 is the only company compute target; 10 GW is a 2027 aspiration. Does the YE26 print use the same energized-nameplate definition, or does "under construction" creep in? Answered by: Q4/YE print with a like-for-like nameplate line.
- **Q3 ARPU and churn after the June price extraction.** ARPU $66 flat q/q (down from $85 Q2'25, $99 in 2023 on international/plan mix); the 18-June hike is the first broad US price extraction and Q2 is pre-hike. Aviation plans doubled to $20k/mo. Rural PMF is real (Reddit: game-changer speeds, congestion/deprioritization the recurring gripe); churn is not evidenced. Amazon Leo's commercial start has slipped to late-2026 (~400 of 3,000+ authorized sats in orbit; enterprise beta since 8 Apr with Verizon/AT&T/Vodafone/JetBlue; Jassy signaling sub-Starlink pricing). Answered by: Q3 ARPU, net adds, Connectivity margin.
- **Is a 90-day CSA an Azure substitute at GW scale?** The rumored MSFT 3 GW lease is publicly unverified. Substitute economics require a named GW-scale, >90-day-duration counterparty on the same 2026–27 MW; otherwise CSAs are bridge capacity for labs that multi-source. Answered by: named counterparty MW + duration in Q3/Q4 disclosures.
- **Tenant-competitor channel conflict.** Anthropic (all of Colossus 1) and Google rent compute from the company whose Grok/Cursor stack competes with them. Do they renew at ramp anniversaries, or exit as Meta's excess-compute resale and neocloud capacity come online? Answered by: renewal/termination disclosure per cohort.
- **Cursor $60B: what does all-stock buy?** Announced 16 June, closed 14 Aug (8-K): 389.3M new Class A shares issued (~3% of pre-deal A+B count), folding into the Grok brand with no standalone entity. Does Cursor's corporate customer base + coding-trace data convert the AI segment from colo-renter into an application-layer attach, or is it a $60B momentum acquisition that moves neither the capital-recovery clock nor campus MW? Answered by: Q4 AI solutions mix ex-infrastructure, retention of Cursor enterprise accounts post-Grok rebrand.
- **Does the power architecture hold at 2 GW+?** Memphis turbines must be removed by 2027 per the regulatory settlement; Terafab's "not expected to use electricity from the grid" is abatement language, not proven islanding at 100M sq ft scale; interconnect queues run 24–48 months. Answered by: permanent-generation buildout milestones vs nameplate adds.
- **Human-capital intensity.** 50–60h baseline, onsite-only, median tenure ~2–2.5y, a consistent Reddit/career-site pattern, **unverified**. Does launch cadence + campus build + constellation ops throughput survive that attrition, or is tenure a P&L-irrelevant culture sensor? Answered by: disclosed attrition or a visible execution miss.
- **Is orbital compute (Starmind AI1) priced as near-term revenue or a 2029+ option?** The 8-June AI1 reveal (120kW avg/150kW peak per satellite; ~1GW/yr orbital *deployment-rate* target by late 2027, "scaling an order of magnitude each year") is folded into the 10GW headline, yet material orbital GW is launch-cadence-gated: ~165–275 Starship flights per orbital GW against one suborbital V3 deployment to date, production starting end-2027, the prospectus dating orbital deployment to "as early as 2028." Is any of the ~$232 avg PT crediting orbital as near-term, or is it correctly option-valued? Answered by: Starship orbital-deploy cadence ramp; Gigasat first AI1 units; any disclosed orbital MW.

## Business Model & Product Description

Three reported segments. Analogy: **Falcon is an owned railroad; Starlink is the toll road built along its tracks; the AI campus is a landlord who erected the building but leases the rolling stock from NVDA, on shorter paper than his own mortgage.**

| Segment (Q2'26) | Revenue | Op. income | Adj. EBITDA | Capex | What it is |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Connectivity | $4,291M | $1,656M (38.6% OM) | $2,597M (60.5%) | $1,367M | Starlink broadband + Starshield. 12.0M subs (+1.7M q/q, 2× YoY), ARPU $66. Consumer $2,485M / ent+gov $1,806M (42.1%). Starshield >$6B multi-year awards. |
| AI | $2,561M | $(1,257)M | $1,146M | $15,828M | xAI/Grok/X: AI solutions & infra $2,194M + ads $367M. Colossus I (Anthropic full buyout) + Colossus II (Memphis TN + Southaven MS; ~1.0 GW combined). Nameplate 1.4 GW. CSAs $14.1B Note 2 + $6.7B early Q3. Cursor $60B all-stock closed 14 Aug (+389.3M Class A). |
| Space | $962M | $(542)M | $(205)M | $1,174M | Launch services $648M + launch & development $314M. 38 launches (10 customer / 28 internal). Starship: Flight 12 (May) suborbital; Flight 13 (24 Jul) first working payload: 20 V3 sats on a burn-up test profile. Space R&D $1,076M. |
| **Total** | **$7,814M** | **$(143)M** | **$3,538M** | **$18,369M** | Net loss $541M. Backlog $47.5B. Cash + marketable $100.0B; debt + leases $39.4B (incl. $25B IG notes, 26 Jun, wtd 5.855%). |

**Connectivity (owned pool).** Full vertical integration: design, build, launch (on internal Falcon at marginal cost), operate. The 2026 constellation lead does not require Starship; Falcon's 28 internal launches per quarter are the factory. V3 satellites (1 Tbps downlink, 160 Gbps uplink, six 400G space lasers each, ~10×/22× V2 Mini) are Starship-dependent for mass deployment but not for the current lead. ARPU decline to $66 reflects international/lower-tier mix; the June hike is the first broad price extraction, with aviation doubling to $20k/mo testing enterprise willingness-to-pay.

**AI (renter pool).** Colossus campuses + CSAs. Rubin-exclusive declaration covers the 2026–27 campus BOM, a procurement decision, not an IDM strategy; Terafab (Grimes County: $16.8B initial, up to $119B four-phase JETI filings, gas+BESS off-grid claim) is aspiration until tool POs. Note 2 definition: contracted sales = non-cancellable enforceable period only; CFO guided +$6.7B contracted over six months ramping from October. Tenants: Anthropic (all of Colossus 1), Google, Reflection AI, unnamed others. Cursor adds an application-layer coding franchise folding into Grok branding.

**Space (shipping, not the residual).** Internal mass-to-orbit is the Starlink factory; customer launch ($648M) is the third-party line. Starship is R&D toward a 99% cost-to-orbit cut and V3 mass deployment, not in 2026 constellation or revenue math.

## Industry Context

Sits in [[Sectors/Neoclouds & GPU-as-a-Service]] as the vertically-integrated entrant beside [[Theses/CRWV - CoreWeave]] and [[Theses/NBIS - Nebius Group]], distinguished on both tails: the only operator with an owned non-AI cash annuity (Connectivity), and the only one selling GW-scale capacity on 90-day paper.

| Layer | Who has leverage | SPCX position |
|---|---|---|
| Accelerators | [[Theses/NVDA - Nvidia]]: Rubin exclusive | 2026–27 campus buy; SPCX is a layer-renter |
| HBM / foundry | [[Theses/000660 - SK Hynix]], [[Theses/TSM - Taiwan Semiconductor]] | Non-cancellable POs upstream of cancellable CSAs |
| WFE / test | [[Theses/AMAT - Applied Materials]], [[Theses/LRCX - Lam Research]], [[Theses/KLA - KLA Corporation]] | Terafab $16.8B→$119B filings = optional WFE demand; aspiration until tool POs |
| Optics / DCI | [[Theses/LITE - Lumentum]] | PhotonCap: first-order value accrues to power/optics/DCI suppliers |
| Foundry / custom silicon | [[Theses/INTC - Intel]] vs TSMC ecosystem | Terafab IDM is a later custom line, not 2026 hardware |
| Neocloud peers | CRWV (MSFT-concentrated, 25.8% interest/rev), NBIS (prepayment-funded, multi-year paper) | SPCX inverts the category: shortest CSA duration, strongest balance sheet ($100B cash, single-digit interest/rev) |
| Compute resale | Meta entering excess-compute resale | Second seller in the CSA market: rate/renewal pressure on cancellable gross |
| Power / siting | Turbines, interconnect queues (24–48mo) | Memphis turbine removal by 2027; off-grid Terafab = abatement text, not proven islanding |
| Connectivity | Amazon Leo (ex-Kuiper): commercial slipped to late-2026; enterprise beta live (Verizon/AT&T/Vodafone/JetBlue/NASA); ~400 of 3,000+ authorized sats in orbit | First credible LEO second source; Starlink priced ahead of it |

Structural force: the Perez frenzy is funding GPU/power/optics over-build across the category. The sector note's leverage ledger puts neoclouds at ~90–100% of drawable capacity with CRWV's interest at the historical 20–25%-of-revenue break line. SPCX enters that reference class with the opposite capital structure (net cash ~$60.6B) but the weakest revenue-duration profile, and a second-order tell: PhotonCap's read that first-order equity value sits in the hardware chain (NVDA, optics, WFE) rather than in the colo layer renting it.

**Orbital datacenters (Starmind AI1): option value, not 2027 pipeline.** The priced narrative folds SpaceX's orbital-compute program into the same "10GW" headline, but it contributes ~zero to any 2027 compute number: the prospectus dates orbital deployment "as early as 2028," and AI1 (120kW avg/150kW peak per satellite, 110m² deployable liquid radiator, Starlink-V3 bus) needs ~8,300 units = ~165–275 dedicated Starship flights *per orbital GW* against a program that has completed one V3 deployment ever (20 sats, suborbital, 24 Jul; first *orbital* deploy targeted late-Aug 2026). Gigasat (Bastrop TX) starts AI1 production end-2027; FCC filing covers ≤1M sats. The value-layer read: orbital is the one place SPCX could re-internalize its scarce complement, owning launch + satellite + solar + laser backhaul end-to-end, a full stack no peer can follow if Starship crosses ~$20M/flight at weekly cadence, so it is a genuine infrastructure-layer option (VLM §3, moat-widening) currently priced as if it were 2027–28 revenue. The terrestrial "10GW" itself is two targets the market conflates: Musk's "tentative 20GW power-and-cooling" (~15GW expected) vs compute "closer to 10 than 5," on a ~5–6× build-rate acceleration (100–130MW/mo realized vs ~667MW/mo required), ~40–50% of Nvidia's global Blackwell output to one customer, and $320–440B of 2027 capex. Base case 4–6GW compute online YE27, with 10GW-online low-probability absent a signed ≥$100B anchor. See [[Research/2026-08-18 - SPCX - 10GW Datacenter Pipeline Feasibility - deep-dive]].

## Management and culture

Hypothesis: Weak fit on [[Lens - Management and Culture]]: Gate 1 passes (launch, constellation, AI campus); Gate 2 fails on the AI pool (avg PT ~$232 already narrates 10 GW). Connectivity conversion is dated (165 Falcon launches in 2025, 12.0M Starlink subs, Q2 Connectivity 60.5% adj. EBITDA would read the same if the stock halved from the $225.64 June 16 high), but that optionality is realized cash, not a ≤0 pipeline. [MC-2] S-1/A 3 Jun: Musk 82.4% vote (Class B 10:1, no sunset); 13 Jan 200M Class B restricted shares (1.0B post May 5-for-1) vest only on market-cap plus a 1-million-person Mars colony, unvested shares vote from grant, not ROIC. Musk 366-day lock-up; Form 4s show no clustered open-market buys. [MC-3]/[MC-7] two orgs: FWP as-of 31 Mar, 21-year top-3 tenure, 12-year VP+, <2% 2025 engineer-applicant accept, onsite 6-day and 50–60h at ~22,000 employees, the launch/Starlink machine, past the ~5,000 matrix ceiling. AI is the other conversion rate: all 11 xAI co-founders gone by 28 Mar; Starlink SVP Nicolls made xAI president in April (engineering reports to him; training compute "embarrassingly low"); Cursor close 14 Aug is a 6-day Grok-brand graft. [MC-6]/[G-10] xAI wipeout plus $13.3B related-party failed sale-leasebacks ($327M Q2 interest) are entropy and waterfall. Swing: Nicolls/Cursor originators get campus P&L authority, or AI stays a Musk overlay.

## Bull Case

Connectivity compounds as an owned annuity: the June hike lifts Q3 ARPU without a churn break, enterprise/Starshield mix (42.1% and rising, >$6B awards) extends duration, and Leo (commercial start slipped to late-2026 with a limited enterprise/gov/mobility initial scope) proves too late and too thin (~400 of 3,000+ authorized sats in orbit vs Starlink's operating constellation + V3 pipeline) to break pricing. The AI campus converts: YE26 prints ≥2 GW on the 1.4 GW definition, CSAs convert to matched-cohort payback or long-duration non-cancellable paper, and a named GW-scale hyperscaler offtake (the unverified MSFT 3 GW, or equivalent) lands on 2026–27 MW, at which point the SemiAnalysis 10 GW / ~$100B-per-GW path acquires a denominator and SPCX becomes the only neocloud whose build is funded by internal cash ($100B + $47.5B backlog) rather than the sector's strained credit stack. Cursor (closed 14 Aug) converts colo into application-layer attach (enterprise coding accounts + Grok distribution), showing up in Q4 AI solutions mix. Starship V3 makes the constellation lead unassailable post-2026 (1 Tbps sats at Starship mass economics). Valuation path: Connectivity annuity (~$10.4B adj. EBITDA run-rate, growing with price extraction) + funded AI option re-rates toward the MS $300 framing as duration disclosure de-risks the second pool.

What has to go right: Connectivity margin band holds, CSA duration prints, YE26 nameplate lands on-definition, no termination cascade, power buildout keeps pace (Memphis turbine replacement, Terafab generation).

## Bear Case

The High-multiple pool is the unproven one. AI capex at $15.8B/quarter builds a depreciating Rubin book ($1.885B quarterly AI D&A and compounding) whose customers can walk on 90 days' notice after ramp, and those customers are competitors (Anthropic, Google) with structural exit incentive the moment Meta's excess-compute resale or neocloud capacity offers an alternative. First termination cascade, or YE26 <2 GW, or a Connectivity margin break, and the ~$1.9T full valuation compresses toward the satellite-broadband + launch stub. Morningstar's $63 FV marks where sum-of-parts-ex-AI pessimism already sits, and the market briefly priced $104.83 (−11% on the capex print) before the unlock-week recovery. Starlink is not immune: ARPU already fell $99→$66, the June extraction tests price-anger-vs-churn with Leo's commercial start slipped to late-2026 but its enterprise beta already carrying carrier distribution (Verizon/AT&T/Vodafone) and Jassy signaling sub-Starlink pricing, and the Jul-2025 global outage + congestion complaints are the product-quality tell in an underserved-rural base with rising alternatives. The 10 GW / $500B-ARR / Terafab / MSFT-largest narrative stack is unverified aspiration priced as pipeline by the bullish half of a $62–$800 dispersion. Supply overhang persists into December (next ~319M unlock 20 Aug; ~40% tradeable by year-end); Cursor's $60B all-stock close issued 389.3M Class A shares (~3% dilution) for an application-layer asset that does not move the capital-recovery clock; related-party interest ($327M Q2) and key-person concentration compound governance discount. World where this loses money: stranded Rubin fleet + Connectivity churn inflection + multiple compression from 34×/59× run-rate toward the stub. No fundamental miss required, just duration disclosure that never arrives.

## Risks

**Thesis risks (the case is wrong)**
- **Capital recovery:** 90-day post-ramp exits < GPU/turbine D&A lives; termination cascade among tenant-competitors; $15.8B/qtr capex uncovered by the non-cancellable book.
- **Connectivity break:** June extraction produces churn; ARPU fails to lift; margin leaves the ~60% band; Leo + carrier distribution takes the marginal rural/enterprise sub.
- **Nameplate miss:** YE26 <2 GW on the 1.4 GW definition; the only company target fails, voiding the build-credibility premise.
- **Jevons non-transfer:** AI colo stays a layer-renter (NVDA/HBM/optics/turbines); the Starlink ownership exception does not repeat; hardware chain captures the value (PhotonCap).
- **Power architecture:** Memphis turbine removal by 2027 + unproven Terafab islanding + 24–48mo interconnect queues cap nameplate growth below target.

**Position risks (thesis right, stock down anyway)**
- **Dispersion/flow regime:** $62–$800 PT range means narrative sets the marginal price; multiple compression from 34×/59× run-rate needs no fundamental miss.
- **Supply:** lock-up tranches into December (next ~319M unlock 20 Aug; ~40% tradeable by year-end); Cursor close added 389.3M Class A shares (~3% count).
- **Key-person / governance:** Musk concentration, $327M Q2 related-party interest, dual-class structure; unverified ~2–2.5y median tenure as execution-fragility signal.
- **Narrative unwind:** 10 GW / Terafab / MSFT-largest headlines deflating hits the multiple even while Connectivity prints.

## Conviction Triggers

- **→ HIGH if:** Connectivity adj. EBITDA margin holds ~60% band through Q4'26 AND CSA duration/payback prints (matched cohort or long-duration non-cancellable amendment) AND YE26 nameplate ≥2 GW on the same definition as the 1.4 GW print
- **→ LOW if:** YE26 nameplate <2 GW same-definition OR first CSA termination cascade OR Connectivity adj. EBITDA margin breaks below ~55% on churn/ARPU
- **→ CLOSE if:** capital-recovery clock fails — disclosed D&A lives exceed demonstrated CSA duration with no long-duration replacement — while Connectivity margin is simultaneously degrading (no residual to fall back on)
